Shape.claim: Games are a mainstream medium in Germany, with 41.2 million people playing, six in ten of those aged 6 to 69, an average age of 38.3, 79 percent of players adults and 46 percent women, per the game Jahresreport 2026, published on 12 August 2026 and covering 2025. The 2025 report had put it at around 37.5 million with an average age of about 40.
Shape.source: game Jahresreport der deutschen Games-Branche 2026, industry association annual report, 12 August 2026

Shape.claim: Germany is a consumption market far more than a production one: games developed in Germany account for about 5.5 percent of domestic games spending, per the study Die Games-Branche in Deutschland 2025.
Shape.source: GamesWirtschaft reporting the game and Goldmedia study, games trade press

Shape.claim: Buying individual games is now a small slice of German games spending: game purchases generated 807 million euros in 2025, down 13 percent, while in-game and in-app purchases held above 4 billion euros.
Shape.source: game Verband annual market figures, industry association

Shape.claim: The German headline is not software spend. Of 9.382 billion euros in 2025, games, meaning purchases plus in-game and in-app spending, are 4.948 billion, hardware is 3.403 billion and online gaming services, subscriptions, cloud and network fees, are 1.031 billion.
Shape.source: game Verband annual market figures, industry association

Market size.claim: The German games market generated around 9.4 billion euros in 2025, a 4 percent increase, per the game association annual market figures based on YouGov and Sensor Tower data.
Market size.source: game Verband annual market figures, industry association

Market size.claim: The association's market figure is not a GfK panel. game builds it from YouGov Shopper, 25,000 representative consumer surveys, NielsenIQ's hardware retail panel and Sensor Tower for mobile, and publishes it each March, the 2025 figure on 26 March 2026, before the August Jahresreport compiles it. The 2025 release restated earlier years after Sensor Tower revised its mobile method and NielsenIQ widened hardware coverage to more physical retail, so take earlier years from the same release.
Market size.source: game Verband annual market figures, 26 March 2026, industry association

Unique to this market.claim: USK ratings are law. Age ratings on games sold in Germany are statutory, not advisory: state youth authority representatives issue the legal USK age label under the Jugendschutzgesetz, and retailers are bound by it.
Unique to this market.card_text: Age ratings are statutory, not advisory
Unique to this market.source: elternguide.online, USK information service

Unique to this market.claim: The largest games event in the world by attendance takes place in Cologne, with around 357,000 visitors and 1,568 exhibitors from 72 countries at gamescom 2025.
Unique to this market.card_text: Hosts the world largest games event by attendance
Unique to this market.source: ZDF heute, public broadcaster news

Unique to this market.claim: Germany keeps an unusually strong attachment to physical media on console: 56 percent of console games sold on Datentraeger (physical discs and cartridges) in 2024, while 99 percent of PC games sold as downloads.
Unique to this market.card_text: Console players prefer physical discs
Unique to this market.source: game Verband download share figures, industry association

Unique to this market.claim: The live German regulatory story is the youth-protection reform, not the old bans. Since 1 May 2021 the reformed Jugendschutzgesetz lets interaction risks count in an age rating, open chats, purchase incentives and gambling-like elements such as loot boxes, and the Bundespruefstelle fuer jugendgefaehrdende Medien became the Bundeszentrale fuer Kinder- und Jugendmedienschutz (BzKJ).
Unique to this market.source: BzKJ announcement of the reform entering into force, federal agency

Unique to this market.claim: Nazi symbols are no longer an automatic bar to a rating. Since 9 August 2018 the USK applies the social-adequacy clause of section 86a of the criminal code to games case by case, after the state youth authorities dropped the requirement that a submission certify it contains no such symbols. The Germany-bans-violent-games story is older still.
Unique to this market.source: GamesWirtschaft report of the USK and OLJB decision, 9 August 2018, games trade press

Where the data lives.claim: game Verband market data. Annual and half year revenue figures for the German market, split by software, hardware, and online services, with methodology notes attached to each release. Lets a researcher anchor any German market size claim to a free primary source.
Where the data lives.source: game Verband market figures, industry association

Where the data lives.claim: GfK Entertainment Games-Charts. Weekly official German games sales charts by platform, published as news posts. Lets a researcher see what actually sells in Germany week by week without buying panel data.
Where the data lives.source: GfK Entertainment, official charts compiler

Where the data lives.claim: JIM-Studie. Annual representative survey of 12 to 19 year olds media use in Germany, running since 1998, free PDF, covering devices, platforms, and gaming alongside wider media behaviour. Lets a researcher ground youth behaviour claims in a public dataset.
Where the data lives.source: mpfs, publicly funded media research consortium

Where the data lives.claim: USK statistics. Annual rating statistics plus a searchable title database of age ratings. Lets a researcher see rating volumes, IARC platform coverage, and which large platforms sit outside the system, the 2025 statistics name Apple and Steam as not connected.
Where the data lives.source: USK, ratings self regulation body

Where the data lives.claim: gamescom figures. Official attendance, exhibitor, floor space, and digital reach numbers for the annual Cologne event, updated each year. Lets a researcher date and size the industry main gathering.
Where the data lives.source: game Verband gamescom page, event co organizer

Where the data lives.claim: The State of Video Gaming, Matthew Ball and Epyllion. A free annual analyst presentation with market sizing, participation and platform charts for most major markets, useful for cross market comparison that no single free source provides. It aggregates many vendors rather than applying one methodology, so treat figures as the analyst assembly they are and cite the underlying source where the deck names one.
Where the data lives.card_text: The State of Video Gaming (Ball, Epyllion)
Where the data lives.source: Matthew Ball, Epyllion, independent analyst, annual presentation

Where the data lives.claim: USK labels do not cover every store. The USK's 2025 statistics name Apple and Steam as large platforms not connected to its system, so a title sold there may carry no USK label even though the label is statutory at retail.
Where the data lives.source: USK annual statistics 2025, ratings self-regulation body

Standing.claim: Europe's largest games market and the fifth largest in the world, according to the game Jahresreport der deutschen Games-Branche 2026, published 12 August 2026.
Standing.source: game Jahresreport der deutschen Games-Branche 2026, industry association annual report, 12 August 2026

known_gaps.gap: Sales charts. GfK Entertainment's weekly charts are a profile card, not a source row; the directory's German sales data row is GSD via Sparkers.
known_gaps.instead: Open the GfK charts from the profile card and say which panel a chart comes from; the two do not share a method.

known_gaps.gap: Federal games funding. The rules have changed more than once and no note here states the current ones.
known_gaps.instead: GamesWirtschaft is the held beat on funding and politics; check its latest piece before quoting a rate, a freeze or a ministry.

known_gaps.gap: Where German players talk. The profile says WhatsApp, YouTube and Facebook carry news, and the community rows are two subreddits.
known_gaps.instead: Use the games-specific subreddit technique, r/zocken not r/de, and the outlets' own forums and Discords the profile names.

known_gaps.gap: Austria and Switzerland. No Austrian or Swiss rows are held, and the statistics are Germany-only while the German-language conversation is not.
known_gaps.instead: Say which country a figure covers when the source is DACH-wide, and do not read a DACH publisher as a German one.

known_gaps.gap: Adult play behaviour. JIM covers ages 12 to 19; no adult play survey row is held beyond the association's own demographics.
known_gaps.instead: Quote the Jahresreport's player figures as the association's, with the year, and use JIM for the young cohort only.

player_population.source: game Verband der deutschen Games-Branche, Jahresreport der deutschen Games-Branche 2026
player_population.definition: The figure counts people in Germany who play computer and video games, stated as "In Deutschland spielen 41,2 Millionen Menschen Computer- und Videospiele." game reports an average player age of 38.3 years, 79 percent aged 18 and over, and a split of 54 percent men and 46 percent women. The data comes from YouGov, with 2026 fieldwork among about 25,000 respondents.

Venues.claim: Do not look for Korean games podcasts by category on Podbbang. The leading Korean podcast platform lists no games or gaming category in its category browser, confirmed August 2026.
Venues.source: Podbbang podcast category browser, platform primary source

Venues.claim: Twitch is dead in Korea, so Twitch data says nothing about Korean streaming. The platform ended its Korean operations on 27 February 2024, about six and a half years after entering, citing network usage fees roughly ten times other countries, a figure Korean network operators dispute.
Venues.card_text: Twitch is dead here, exited Feb 2024
Venues.source: KISO Journal, internet self governance organisation publication

Venues.claim: Live game streaming runs through three platforms: SOOP, formerly AfreecaTV, Naver 치지직 (Chzzk), launched in December 2023 as the Twitch successor, and YouTube Live.
Venues.source: 국민일보 games policy column, national daily

Venues.claim: Do not assert the scale of the anonymous boards without checking. 디시인사이드 (DC Inside) galleries, 에펨코리아 (FMKorea) and 아카라이브 (Arca.live) are commonly described as major games discussion venues, but their current scale and games activity could not be verified to standard.
Venues.source: No source meeting this directory's standard

Standing.claim: The world's fourth largest games market, according to the 2025 White Paper on Korean Games (대한민국 게임백서), Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism and KOCCA, March 2026.
Standing.source: 2025 대한민국 게임백서, government and public agency annual, reported by Digital Today, named tech outlet

Standing.claim: The fourth-place world rank is the white paper's own. It is a 7.2 percent share of a world market the paper estimates at 220.071 billion dollars for 2024, measured against Korean industry sales rather than consumer spend, so it is not the rank a Newzoo or Ball table gives, and the two do not belong in one sentence.
Standing.source: Digital Today report of the 2025 White Paper on Korean Games, named news outlet

Market size.claim: Domestic games industry revenue is 23.8515 trillion won in 2024, up 3.9 percent year on year, per the 2025 White Paper on Korean Games.
Market size.source: 2025 대한민국 게임백서, reported by Digital Today, named tech outlet

Market size.claim: The white paper's revenue is industry sales, not consumer spend. Its 23.8515 trillion won for 2024 is sales by platform, mobile 14.071 trillion, PC 6.0094 trillion, console 1.1836 trillion and arcade 275.9 billion won, with PC bang and arcade venue takings inside the PC and arcade lines. Do not set it beside a Newzoo or Sensor Tower estimate without saying which basis each is on.
Market size.source: Digital Today report of the 2025 White Paper on Korean Games, named news outlet

Shape.claim: Korea primarily makes and exports games. 2024 exports are 8.503 billion dollars, up 1.3 percent, against imports of 245.6 million dollars. Export destinations are led by China at 29.7 percent, Southeast Asia at 20.6 percent, North America at 19.5 percent and Japan at 8.3 percent.
Shape.source: 2025 대한민국 게임백서, reported by 문화일보, national daily

Shape.claim: Games are no longer a majority pastime in Korea. The 2025 game user survey puts the game usage rate at 50.2 percent, down 9.7 percentage points in one year, with a five year annual growth rate of minus 6.8 percent. KOCCA describes the market as reorganising around core users.
Shape.source: KOCCA 2025 게임이용자 실태조사 press release, government agency survey

Shape.claim: Korea is turning more PC heavy while shrinking. Among game users in 2025, mobile reaches 89.1 percent but is falling, while PC rises to 58.1 percent and console to 28.6 percent, and daily PC playtime is at its highest level in five years.
Shape.source: KOCCA 2025 게임이용자 실태조사 press release, government agency survey

Shape.claim: The industry employs 87,576 people in 2024, up 3.1 percent, with 62 percent in production and distribution rather than retail.
Shape.source: 2025 대한민국 게임백서, reported by Digital Today, named tech outlet

Shape.claim: The user survey's platform rates overlap and do not sum. Its 50.2 percent is the share of people aged 10 to 69 who played in the past year; mobile 89.1, PC 58.1 and console 28.6 percent are shares of those users rather than of Koreans, and a person on two platforms is counted in both, so they are not a device split.
Shape.source: KOCCA, 2025 Game User Survey (게임이용자 실태조사), government agency

Shape.claim: KOCCA's two annuals carry different years, so quote the year with the figure. The 2025 White Paper on Korean Games, published in March 2026, reports 2024 revenue and exports; the 2025 Game User Survey, published on 18 December 2025, reports play in the year to its fieldwork. There is no white-paper revenue figure for 2025 yet.
Shape.source: KOCCA press release for the 2025 Game User Survey, 22 December 2025, government agency

Press structure.claim: News distribution in Korea routes through portals. Online portals such as Naver are the most widely used news source, and admission to a portal directly affects an outlet traffic, influence and advertising revenue through Naver partnership evaluation system, which suspended activity in 2023 and was relaunched in February 2026. Portal news use is nonetheless declining each year since 2021 as video and short form use rises.
Press structure.source: Reuters Institute Digital News Report 2026, South Korea page, academic institute

Press structure.claim: The largest games site, 인벤 (Inven), is a fused community and webzine, operating forums and an editorial newsroom in one property, and by its own account has supplied esports news to Naver since 2013.
Press structure.source: Inven corporate profile, company self description reproduced on the Gamejob recruiting service

Press structure.claim: Do not assert Ruliweb's ownership history. 루리웹 (Ruliweb), the largest console-focused community, is widely described as having passed through a series of portal owners before becoming independent in 2016, but that history could not be verified beyond community wikis and the site's own posts.
Press structure.source: No source meeting this directory's standard

Press structure.claim: Korea press structure is community and media fusion plus portal gatekept distribution. The biggest games venues are community boards with newsrooms attached, and an outlet reach depends on admission to a portal. This is an interpretation resting on the rows above.
Press structure.source: Reuters Institute Digital News Report 2026, South Korea page, plus the rows above

Unique to this market.claim: Every game distributed in Korea requires a pre release age classification, issued by the Game Rating and Administration Committee (게임물관리위원회, GRAC), the delegated private classification body, or platform self classification, and every rating decision is searchable in a public database.
Unique to this market.card_text: Every game needs a pre release age rating
Unique to this market.source: GRAC official site, statutory classification body

Unique to this market.claim: Loot box odds disclosure is law. From 22 March 2024 the Game Industry Promotion Act requires games to display probability item odds in game and in advertising, with violations punishable by up to two years imprisonment or a 20 million won fine.
Unique to this market.card_text: Loot box odds disclosure is law
Unique to this market.source: Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism decision, reported by ZDNet Korea, named tech outlet

Unique to this market.claim: HOLD: do not report a GRAC reorganisation as decided. Reports indicate the current administration is moving to abolish or reorganise GRAC and establish a game promotion agency, which if enacted changes the rating system, but this could not be verified beyond a community wiki. Confirm at ministry or Assembly sources first.
Unique to this market.source: No source meeting this directory's standard

Unique to this market.claim: Korean mobile spend routes overwhelmingly through Google Play, which Sensor Tower own Korea report projects at 75 percent of an estimated 5.3 billion dollars in 2025 in app purchase revenue.
Unique to this market.card_text: Mobile spend routes through Google Play, not the App Store
Unique to this market.source: Sensor Tower Korea market report, vendor own free publication

Unique to this market.claim: State whether One Store is in scope. Sensor Tower's Korea report says all its data excludes third-party Android markets, so its 5.3 billion dollar projection for 2025 and its 75 percent Google Play share cover the App Store and Google Play only; One Store, Korea's domestic Android store, is outside it and outside any global tracker's default view.
Unique to this market.source: Sensor Tower Korea market report, November 2025, vendor own free publication

Unique to this market.claim: The shutdown law is gone. The midnight-to-6am ban on under-16s' online play under the Youth Protection Act ended at midnight on 31 December 2021, after the National Assembly repealed it in November 2021, and was replaced by a choice system in which under-18s or their guardians pick their own hours. English coverage still describes Korea as the curfew country.
Unique to this market.source: The Korea Herald, 31 December 2021, national daily

Unique to this market.claim: Foreign publishers need a domestic agent. Since 23 October 2025, under Article 31-2 of the Game Industry Promotion Act as amended on 22 October 2024, an overseas game company with annual sales of 1 trillion won or more, or 100,000 average domestic users over three months, must designate a domestic agent; the Game Rating and Administration Committee checks, and the fine for failing to is up to 20 million won.
Unique to this market.source: Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism press release, 24 April 2025, government body

Where the data lives.claim: 대한민국 게임백서 (White Paper on Korean Games). KOCCA annual gives industry revenue, exports by destination, employment and Korea world share, and the full PDF is free.
Where the data lives.card_text: 대한민국 게임백서 (White Paper on Korean Games)
Where the data lives.source: KOCCA 산업백서 index, government agency

Where the data lives.claim: 게임이용자 실태조사 (Game User Survey). KOCCA annual survey of 10,000 people aged 10 to 69 gives game usage rates, platform splits, playtime and spending, the standard free source on who plays in Korea.
Where the data lives.source: KOCCA press release, government agency survey

Where the data lives.claim: GRAC 등급분류 database. The regulator searchable database of every rating decision, including self classified games, lets a researcher confirm any game legal release status, rating and rating history in Korea.
Where the data lives.source: 게임물관리위원회 (GRAC), statutory classification body

Where the data lives.claim: KRAFTON investor relations. Quarterly earnings releases and periodic reports give platform level and IP level revenue splits, an example of the disclosure depth available from Korea listed publishers.
Where the data lives.source: KRAFTON, primary corporate disclosure

Where the data lives.claim: 글로벌 게임산업 트렌드 (Global Game Industry Trends). KOCCA free bimonthly briefing covers overseas market, policy and company developments including emerging markets, written for Korean companies going abroad.
Where the data lives.card_text: 글로벌 게임산업 트렌드 (Global Game Industry Trends)
Where the data lives.source: KOCCA, government agency bimonthly

Where the data lives.claim: The State of Video Gaming, Matthew Ball and Epyllion. A free annual analyst presentation with market sizing, participation and platform charts for most major markets, useful for cross market comparison that no single free source provides. It aggregates many vendors rather than applying one methodology, so treat figures as the analyst assembly they are and cite the underlying source where the deck names one.
Where the data lives.card_text: The State of Video Gaming (Ball, Epyllion)
Where the data lives.source: Matthew Ball, Epyllion, independent analyst, annual presentation

known_gaps.gap: PC bang share. No PC bang tracker is held, and the ones that exist publish share of usage hours, not revenue.
known_gaps.instead: Read a PC bang share as what is played in public, not what is paid for. Venue takings sit inside the white paper's PC line.

known_gaps.gap: What players think. No Korean user-review venue is held, and the community boards are unverified for scale.
known_gaps.instead: Use the Naver-not-Google and translate-the-SERP techniques for reaction; read Inven and ThisIsGame as press with communities attached; treat a board thread as temperature, never as size.

known_gaps.gap: Sell-side research. The directory holds one analyst's public Telegram digest, not the brokerage sector notes themselves.
known_gaps.instead: Follow the Telegram technique to the analysts, then ask each for the note; the digests say which house wrote what.

known_gaps.gap: Arca.live has no source row. The profile names it beside DC Inside and FMKorea as unverified.
known_gaps.instead: Check a gallery's recent post dates before naming it as a venue.

player_population.source: 한국콘텐츠진흥원 KOCCA and 문화체육관광부, 2025 게임이용자 실태조사
player_population.definition: KOCCA reports a game usage rate of 50.2 percent among people in Korea aged 10 to 69 who played in the previous twelve months. It publishes no headcount. The figure here approximates that rate against the population of that age group. The population base is not yet recorded, so the rate is the sourced part and the headcount is indicative.

Standing.claim: Do not look for Japan's world rank in a Japanese source, because none states one. CESA and the Famitsu Game White Paper 2026 publish a domestic market size and a global total, 32.1024 trillion yen or 214.56 billion dollars for 2025, in regional tables rather than a country ranking. A rank for Japan has to come from an analyst outside Japan, on that analyst's basis.
Standing.source: Kadokawa ASCII Research Institute release for Famitsu Game White Paper 2026, 6 August 2026, publisher release

Market size.claim: The domestic game content market is 2.5885 trillion yen in 2025, up 8.0 percent year on year, per the Famitsu Game White Paper 2026, announced 6 August 2026. The 2024 figure was 2.3961 trillion yen.
Market size.source: Famitsu Game White Paper 2026, Kadokawa ASCII Research Institute, publisher release

Shape.claim: Japan game population is 54.75 million in 2024, a slight decline from 55.53 million the previous year, with 42.78 million on mobile, 29.51 million on console and 14.52 million on PC. Console players roughly double PC players.
Shape.source: CESA Game Industry Report 2025, industry association annual

Shape.claim: Multi device play is near half the player base. 24.78 million people play on two or more of console, PC and mobile in 2024, which the publisher highlights as a marked increase.
Shape.source: Famitsu Game White Paper 2025, Kadokawa ASCII Research Institute, publisher release

Shape.claim: Japan makes and exports games as well as buying them. Content industry exports reach 5.8 trillion yen in 2023, of which games are 62 percent, a total CESA states already exceeds Japan semiconductor and steel exports.
Shape.source: CESA Game Industry Report 2025, industry association

Shape.claim: The two annuals carry different years for the same series, so quote the year with the figure. Famitsu's white paper lands in August with the previous calendar year: the 2026 edition gives 56.39 million players for 2025, up 3.0 percent on 54.75 million for 2024. CESA's report lands in December with the year before that: the 2025 edition still carries 2024. The gap between them is the calendar, not the method.
Shape.source: Famitsu Game White Paper 2026, Kadokawa ASCII Research Institute, publisher release

Press structure.claim: The two flagship legacy games media brands, Famitsu and Dengeki, are operated by a single company, KADOKAWA Game Linkage, inside the KADOKAWA group.
Press structure.source: KADOKAWA Game Linkage company site (出資比率 株式会社KADOKAWA 100%), primary corporate disclosure

Press structure.claim: One research house sits behind both national annuals. Kadokawa ASCII Research Institute publishes the Famitsu Game White Paper and produces and sells the CESA Game Industry Report under commission from CESA. Treat the two as one methodology family rather than two independent measurements, and credit the institute, not an older producer name.
Press structure.source: KADOKAWA group release for CESA Game Industry Report 2025, primary corporate disclosure

Press structure.claim: 4Gamer.net, one of the largest games news sites, is operated by Aetas, a subsidiary of Digital Hearts Holdings, a debugging and QA vendor whose clients are the game publishers the site covers. Digital Hearts acquired Aetas for 800 million yen in 2012.
Press structure.source: ITmedia NEWS report, named tech news outlet

Press structure.claim: AUTOMATON, a leading independent voice games site, is operated by Active Gaming Media, an Osaka localization, debugging and promotion vendor that also runs the indie games publisher PLAYISM.
Press structure.source: Game Creators interview with Active Gaming Media, trade careers media

Press structure.claim: The defining pattern of the Japanese games press is vendor ownership rather than closure. The largest outlets sit inside companies that sell services to the publishers they cover, media and data publishing at KADOKAWA, QA at Digital Hearts, localization at Active Gaming Media. This is an interpretation resting on the three ownership claims above.
Press structure.source: KADOKAWA group release, primary corporate disclosure, plus the ownership rows above

Venues.claim: YouTube reaches 81.5 percent of Japanese people aged 13 to 79 and is the default open video venue. TikTok reaches 36.7 percent.
Venues.card_text: YouTube, the default open video venue
Venues.source: Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications media usage survey, government survey

Venues.claim: Do not default to Facebook for Japanese games talk. X reaches 44.7 percent of people aged 13 to 79 and is the main open text venue; Facebook reaches 27.0 percent, the lowest of the platforms measured. The guidance rests on reach, not on a games-specific measure.
Venues.card_text: X, the main open text venue. Facebook is marginal
Venues.source: Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications media usage survey, government survey

Venues.claim: LINE conversations are private. It reaches 92.9 percent of people aged 13 to 79, more than any other service, and none of its conversation is publicly searchable, so it is not a listening venue. That LINE is private is a reading of the product type, not a survey finding.
Venues.card_text: LINE, private messaging, not publicly searchable
Venues.source: Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications media usage survey, government survey

Venues.claim: Niconico, historically a central Japanese video venue, is owned by Dwango, a KADOKAWA subsidiary. A ransomware attack on 8 June 2024 took the service offline for about two months, with full relaunch on 5 August 2024.
Venues.source: KADOKAWA group system failure disclosure, primary corporate disclosure

Venues.claim: Do not name 5channel as a live games venue without checking it yourself. The anonymous boards under 5ちゃんねる (formerly 2channel) are commonly described as one, but their current scale, ownership and games-board activity could not be verified to standard from outside Japan.
Venues.source: No source meeting this directory's standard

Venues.claim: The MIC survey measures reach, not games use. Its percentages say how many people aged 13 to 79 use each platform at all, so use them to choose which venues to read and not to size a games audience on any of them.
Venues.source: Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications media usage survey, government survey

Unique to this market.claim: Japan publishes free weekly estimated unit sales for packaged console software and hardware. Famitsu releases a top 10 with unit counts every week, with fuller rankings following days later.
Unique to this market.card_text: Free weekly console sales rankings
Unique to this market.source: Famitsu.com weekly sales report, games trade media

Unique to this market.claim: The national annuals are paid, and only their headlines are free. The CESA Game Industry Report is 55,000 yen; the Famitsu Game White Paper 2026 is 48,400 yen as a PDF, 57,200 as a book and 99,000 as the set. What circulates free is each publisher's press release.
Unique to this market.card_text: National data annuals are paid, 48,000 to 99,000 yen
Unique to this market.source: CESA official report page, industry association

Unique to this market.claim: Platform player counts overlap and do not sum. A person who plays on two platforms is counted on both, so the mobile, console and PC figures add up to far more than the game population; 24.78 million people were counted on two or more platforms in 2024.
Unique to this market.card_text: Platform player counts overlap and do not sum
Unique to this market.source: Famitsu Game White Paper 2025, Kadokawa ASCII Research Institute

Unique to this market.claim: The Famitsu weekly chart is not total sales. It estimates units of packaged software, download cards and pre-installed copies; purchases made directly on a digital store are outside it, and so are mobile and PC. A chart position understates a digital-heavy release.
Unique to this market.source: Famitsu.com weekly sales report, games trade media

Where the data lives.claim: CESA ゲーム産業レポート (Game Industry Report). The industry association annual gives national game population by platform, a global market estimate, user survey results and industry data, with headline figures free in each December release.
Where the data lives.card_text: CESA ゲーム産業レポート (Game Industry Report)
Where the data lives.source: CESA, industry association

Where the data lives.claim: ファミ通ゲーム白書 (Famitsu Game White Paper). The annual gives domestic and global market sizing, platform breakdowns and user survey data, with headline figures free in each August release. The mobile edition global data is supervised by Sensor Tower.
Where the data lives.card_text: ファミ通ゲーム白書 (Famitsu Game White Paper)
Where the data lives.source: Kadokawa ASCII Research Institute, publisher release

Where the data lives.claim: ファミ通 weekly sales rankings. Weekly estimated unit sales for packaged console software and hardware in Japan, free, published every week.
Where the data lives.card_text: ファミ通 weekly sales rankings
Where the data lives.source: Famitsu.com, games trade media

Where the data lives.claim: 任天堂 IR (Nintendo investor relations). Primary corporate disclosure with regional sales splits, hardware and software unit sales by quarter, cumulative top title sales and long run historical data.
Where the data lives.source: Nintendo Co., Ltd., primary corporate disclosure

Where the data lives.claim: 経済産業省 (METI) entertainment and creative industries strategy. The June 2025 government action plan analyses the games business segment by segment, console, PC, mobile and esports, with export policy context.
Where the data lives.card_text: 経済産業省 (METI) creative industries strategy
Where the data lives.source: METI, government body

Where the data lives.claim: 総務省 (MIC) media usage survey. The annual government survey gives platform usage rates by age band for LINE, X, YouTube, Instagram, TikTok and Facebook, the standard free source for venue triage in Japan.
Where the data lives.source: Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications, government body

Where the data lives.claim: The State of Video Gaming, Matthew Ball and Epyllion. A free annual analyst presentation with market sizing, participation and platform charts for most major markets, useful for cross market comparison that no single free source provides. It aggregates many vendors rather than applying one methodology, so treat figures as the analyst assembly they are and cite the underlying source where the deck names one.
Where the data lives.card_text: The State of Video Gaming (Ball, Epyllion)
Where the data lives.source: Matthew Ball, Epyllion, independent analyst, annual presentation

Where the data lives.claim: There is no CESA white paper any more. The CESA ゲーム白書 ran to 2023 and was replaced in 2024 by the CESA ゲーム産業レポート (Game Industry Report), out each December; the 2025 edition was released on 15 December 2025 at 55,000 yen. Anything that cites the white paper is citing a pre-2024 source.
Where the data lives.source: CESA industry research page, industry association

known_gaps.gap: How people play. Spend per head, session length, solo against social play and the device mix by age are not held: the profile counts players and the directory holds no consumer-survey rows for Japan.
known_gaps.instead: The user-survey chapters of the CESA report and the Famitsu white paper are behind the paywall. Japanese research houses publish free consumer surveys as PDFs; use the filetype:pdf technique on ゲーム 利用実態 調査 and treat each as that house's sample.

known_gaps.gap: What players think. No Japanese user-review or reader-review venue is held, and nothing here measures sentiment.
known_gaps.instead: For reaction to a launch use the Yahoo! Japan realtime and lang:ja techniques; for reviews open the store page or the outlet's own review section directly.

known_gaps.gap: Who spends. Payer demographics, the share of spend from heavy payers and gacha spend by age are not held. Publisher IR gives revenue without demographics.
known_gaps.instead: The Famitsu white paper's user survey is the paid source. Read any free figure on payers as one vendor's panel.

known_gaps.gap: Mobile revenue tracking is not tagged to Japan. Sensor Tower and AppMagic are Global rows, so a JP-filtered search does not return them.
known_gaps.instead: Search the Data group without a market filter. The Famitsu white paper's mobile chapter is Sensor Tower-supervised, which is one house's estimate, not a second one.

known_gaps.gap: Arcades and amusement. No source for arcade revenue is held.
known_gaps.instead: Sega Sammy and Bandai Namco report amusement segments in their IR, each on its own definition; the directory holds both IR rows.

known_gaps.gap: Video channels carry no market tag by design, so a JP-filtered search returns none.
known_gaps.instead: Search channels by language Japanese instead.

player_population.source: 一般社団法人コンピュータエンターテインメント協会 CESA, CESAゲーム産業レポート2025 (CESA Game Industry Report 2025)
player_population.definition: The figure is the game population, ゲーム人口, stated as 5,475万人, against 5,553万人 the previous year, which CESA calls a slight decline, 微減. The platform split is 4,278万 mobile, 2,951万 home console and 1,452万 PC, which sum well above the total, so a person playing on more than one platform is counted in each. The page does not state the age range surveyed or the fieldwork method.

Standing.claim: Do not look for a Chinese world rank in the in-market source, because it states none. The 2025 China Game Industry Report summary presents domestic revenue and user figures without a ranking claim. A rank comes from an analyst outside China, on that analyst's basis.
Standing.source: 2025年中国游戏产业报告 summary as distributed by Xinhua, state news agency

Market size.claim: Domestic games market actual sales revenue is 350.789 billion yuan in 2025, up 7.68 percent, with a user base of 683 million, both record highs, per the 2025 China Game Industry Report.
Market size.source: CGIGC annual report via Xinhua, state news agency

Market size.claim: The 350.789 billion yuan is the committee's actual sales revenue, published before the year it describes had ended. The report calls the figure 实际销售收入, and the 2025 report was released on 19 December 2025 with the full-year 2025 figure; it does not say how the remaining days are counted. It is not a consumer-spend estimate from Newzoo or Niko and not a publisher's net revenue after channel fees, so name the basis with the number.
Market size.source: 2025 China Game Industry Report as distributed by Xinhua, 19 December 2025, state news agency

Shape.claim: Play is mobile dominated with a fast shifting periphery. Mobile takes 257.076 billion yuan of the 2025 domestic total, roughly 73 percent, client PC games take 78.16 billion yuan, console games take 8.362 billion yuan growing 86.33 percent in a third straight year of rapid growth, and web games decline for a tenth consecutive year.
Shape.source: CGIGC annual report via 证券时报, securities daily

Shape.claim: China primarily makes what it plays and exports at scale. Self developed games earn 291.095 billion yuan domestically in 2025, up 11.64 percent, and 20.455 billion dollars overseas, up 10.23 percent, a sixth consecutive year above 100 billion yuan, with the United States, Japan and Korea taking over half of overseas revenue.
Shape.source: CGIGC annual report via 蓝鲸新闻 on 东方财富, financial news service

Shape.claim: The internet base behind the market is 1.123 billion netizens at 79.7 percent penetration as of June 2025, per the CNNIC 56th statistical report.
Shape.source: CNNIC 第56次中国互联网络发展状况统计报告 via China Daily, state media

Shape.claim: Do not add overseas revenue to the domestic market. The 20.455 billion dollars self-developed games earn overseas is reported separately from the 350.789 billion yuan domestic figure; a chart that folds a Chinese publisher's overseas earnings into the Chinese market is measuring Chinese companies, not Chinese players.
Shape.source: CGIGC annual report via Xinhua, state news agency

Shape.claim: Mini-program games are their own line. The report gives 53.535 billion yuan for mini-program games beside 257.076 billion yuan for mobile games, and the summary does not say whether one sits inside the other, so do not add the two and do not read the mini-game growth as extra to mobile.
Shape.source: CGIGC annual report via 证券时报, securities daily

Unique to this market.claim: Every online game requires prior approval and a publication number, the 版号 (banhao), from the National Press and Publication Administration before commercial release. Approvals are published in monthly public lists, domestic and imported games listed separately.
Unique to this market.card_text: Every game needs a state licence (版号)
Unique to this market.source: 国家新闻出版署 (NPPA) game approval results index, state regulator

Unique to this market.claim: Minors may be served online games only from 20:00 to 21:00 on Fridays, Saturdays, Sundays and legal holidays, one hour per day, and every game must connect to the national real name anti addiction verification system, under NPPA notice 国新出发〔2021〕14号, in force since 1 September 2021.
Unique to this market.card_text: Minors: one hour, Fridays, weekends and holidays only
Unique to this market.source: 国家新闻出版署 notice text on the State Council portal, primary legal text

Unique to this market.claim: Minor spending is capped by age band under the 2019 anti addiction notice, no paid services under age 8, single top ups capped at 50 yuan and monthly at 200 yuan for ages 8 to 15, and 100 yuan and 400 yuan for ages 16 and 17.
Unique to this market.card_text: Minor spending capped by age band
Unique to this market.source: 21世纪经济报道 compliance testing of 20 mobile games, business daily

Unique to this market.claim: The Regulations on the Protection of Minors in Cyberspace (未成年人网络保护条例), in force since 1 January 2024, prohibit providing game account rental and sale services to minors, with fines and suspension penalties for violations.
Unique to this market.source: Xinhua reporting citing the regulation, state news agency

Unique to this market.claim: Foreign games reach the market through a separate imported game approval track with a domestic publishing unit of record on each approval, and imported approvals run far below domestic ones, 977 domestic against 98 imported in 2023.
Unique to this market.card_text: Foreign games need a domestic publisher
Unique to this market.source: NPPA approval data via 证券时报, securities daily

Unique to this market.claim: Sensor Tower's China figures are App Store only. Google Play is not available in China and Sensor Tower's rankings exclude third-party Android stores, which its own charts label China (App Store only), so an iOS-derived China figure covers one store in a market where Android spend runs through domestic stores.
Unique to this market.source: Sensor Tower blog, worldwide revenue ranking with its China footnote, September 2022, vendor publication

Unique to this market.claim: The minors rules matter for compliance, not for the revenue model. Tencent says minors were 0.2 percent of its domestic game time in 2024, a record low, so read the play-hour and spending caps as regulatory exposure and enforcement cost rather than as a driver of revenue.
Unique to this market.source: Yicai report of Tencent Games' announcement, 24 February 2025, financial news outlet

Press structure.claim: Read every mainland Chinese source as operating under censorship. Independent games journalism in the sense used elsewhere in this directory does not exist in mainland China; all domestic media and platforms operate under government censorship requirements.
Press structure.source: Freedom House, Freedom on the Net 2024 China report, US research NGO

Press structure.claim: The authoritative market data layer is fused with the industry body and the state. The annual industry report is produced by CGIGC, a committee of the China Audio-Video and Digital Publishing Association, launched at the industry annual conference and distributed by the state news agency Xinhua.
Press structure.source: Xinhua distribution of the 2025 report, state news agency

Press structure.claim: A business to business trade media layer covers the market for practitioners. GameLook, an industry trade site, republishes official report texts in full alongside commercial and product coverage.
Press structure.source: GameLook, industry trade media

Press structure.claim: An enthusiast and community layer serves consumer audiences, including 机核 (GCores), a games media and community site, and portal era sites such as 17173.
Press structure.source: 机核 GCores article page, games media and community site

Press structure.claim: The space that independent journalism occupies elsewhere is filled by industry service trade media, platform native channels, and official association publishing. This is an interpretation resting on the rows above.
Press structure.source: Freedom House country assessment plus the rows above

Venues.claim: Do not reach for the international platforms when researching Chinese games discourse. Facebook, X, Instagram, YouTube, WhatsApp and Telegram are blocked, Reddit since August 2018, all languages of Wikipedia since April 2019, and Google search since 2012.
Venues.source: Freedom House, Freedom on the Net 2024 China report, US research NGO

Venues.claim: Domestic platforms fill the space the blocks created. Freedom House attributes the growth of local products such as WeChat (微信) and Sina Weibo (新浪微博) directly to the long standing blocks on international platforms, and both operate under government censorship demands.
Venues.card_text: WeChat and Weibo fill the space
Venues.source: Freedom House, Freedom on the Net 2024 China report, US research NGO

Venues.claim: Mini program games running inside super app ecosystems are a venue and a market at once, earning 53.535 billion yuan in 2025, up 34.39 percent.
Venues.source: CGIGC annual report via 证券时报, securities daily

Venues.claim: Disclose bilibili's dual role wherever you cite it as a venue. bilibili operates as a major video community and simultaneously holds game publication approvals as a licensed publisher, with both imported and domestic titles on 2025 approval lists.
Venues.source: 证券时报 coverage of August 2025 approval lists, securities daily

Venues.claim: Do not assert the Chinese streaming and forum layer without verification. Huya, Douyu and Douyin live, and the forums NGA, TapTap and Baidu Tieba, are widely described as core games venues, but their current scale and games activity could not be verified to standard from outside the country.
Venues.source: No source meeting this directory's standard

Where the data lives.claim: NPPA game approval lists. The regulator monthly public lists let a researcher confirm whether any game is licensed for the Chinese market, when it was approved, and which domestic publisher holds the approval, with domestic and imported tracks listed separately.
Where the data lives.source: 国家新闻出版署 (NPPA), state regulator

Where the data lives.claim: 中国游戏产业报告 (China Game Industry Report). CGIGC annual gives domestic revenue, user scale, platform splits, self developed and overseas revenue, released each December with the headline summary free through state media and trade press.
Where the data lives.card_text: 中国游戏产业报告 (China Game Industry Report)
Where the data lives.source: CGIGC via Xinhua, state news agency

Where the data lives.claim: CNNIC 中国互联网络发展状况统计报告 (Statistical Report on Internet Development in China). The twice yearly state statistical report gives netizen scale, penetration, and user counts for major application categories including online games.
Where the data lives.card_text: CNNIC 统计报告 (Internet Development Statistical Report)
Where the data lives.source: CNNIC via China Daily, state media

Where the data lives.claim: Tencent investor relations. Quarterly results and annual reports from the market largest publisher give games revenue split domestic and international, deferred revenue, and title level commentary, in English and Chinese.
Where the data lives.source: Tencent Holdings, primary corporate disclosure, HKEX 700

Where the data lives.claim: 中国政府网 policy library (zhengce). Primary regulatory texts governing games, including the minors play time notice, are hosted in full in the central government policy database, the citation of record for any regulatory claim.
Where the data lives.source: 中国政府网, State Council portal, primary legal texts

Where the data lives.claim: Freedom House, Freedom on the Net, China report. The annual assessment documents which international platforms are blocked and how content control operates, the standard free reference for platform accessibility when planning China research.
Where the data lives.card_text: Freedom House, Freedom on the Net
Where the data lives.source: Freedom House, US research NGO, annual

Where the data lives.claim: The State of Video Gaming, Matthew Ball and Epyllion. A free annual analyst presentation with market sizing, participation and platform charts for most major markets, useful for cross market comparison that no single free source provides. It aggregates many vendors rather than applying one methodology, so treat figures as the analyst assembly they are and cite the underlying source where the deck names one.
Where the data lives.card_text: The State of Video Gaming (Ball, Epyllion)
Where the data lives.source: Matthew Ball, Epyllion, independent analyst, annual presentation

known_gaps.gap: Communities. One community row, Heybox, whose audience figures are the operator's own, and the forum and streaming layer named in the profile is unverified for scale.
known_gaps.instead: TapTap is held as a data row and store; treat any board or streaming figure as that platform's own claim.

known_gaps.gap: Android store data. No held source covers third-party Android stores or direct distribution, and Sensor Tower is App Store only.
known_gaps.instead: Niko Partners, held and paid, and Gamma Data, the report's own partner, are the routes beyond iOS; say which store set a mobile figure covers.

known_gaps.gap: Private publishers. The private giants file nothing, and the directory holds Tencent and NetEase investor relations only.
known_gaps.instead: Read any figure for a private Chinese publisher as an estimate, however precise it looks, and name whose.

known_gaps.gap: Approval history. The NPPA monthly lists are held; no note summarises the pauses between them.
known_gaps.instead: Count the gaps from the lists themselves rather than quoting a freeze from memory.

known_gaps.gap: Trade press. GameLook is cited in the profile and has no source row; the CN press rows are nine.
known_gaps.instead: Open it from the profile's press-structure row, and read the B2B trade layer as republishing official texts alongside its own coverage.

player_population.source: 中国音像与数字出版协会 China Audio-Video and Digital Publishing Association, 2025年中国游戏产业报告 2025 China Game Industry Report
player_population.definition: The figure is the game user base, 用户规模, stated as 6.83亿. The report does not define what counts as a user, over what period, or for what age range. It is a headline total published without a stated methodology.

Standing.claim: Do not look for a US world rank in the industry body's data, because the ESA states none. Its 2026 Essential Facts report and its February 2026 spending release call video games the country's most popular form of entertainment and quantify spending, but neither ranks the US among markets. A rank comes from an analyst, on that analyst's basis.
Standing.source: ESA annual consumer spending release, industry association

Market size.claim: Consumer spending on video games in the United States totals 60.8 billion dollars in 2025, comprising 52.4 billion on content, 5.4 billion on hardware and 2.9 billion on accessories, per the ESA with Circana and Sensor Tower.
Market size.source: ESA annual consumer spending release, industry association

Market size.claim: The 60.8 billion dollar figure is consumer spend on one stated basis. The ESA compiles it from Circana and Sensor Tower: 52.4 billion of content, covering physical and digital full games, DLC and microtransactions and subscriptions across console, cloud, mobile, portable, PC and VR, with mobile at 26.7 billion from Sensor Tower, plus 5.4 billion of hardware and 2.9 billion of accessories. The release lists what is counted and advertising is not on the list, so a figure that includes mobile ad revenue is on a different basis.
Market size.source: ESA annual consumer spending release, 11 February 2026, corrected March 2026, industry association

Shape.claim: 212.3 million Americans play video games every week in 2026, up 3 percent or 7.2 million year on year, with the gender split near even at 53 percent men and 46 percent women.
Shape.source: ESA 2026 Essential Facts report, industry association survey with YouGov

Shape.claim: The player base is middle aged and long tenured. The average player is 37 years old, 71 percent of millennials, 56 percent of Gen X and 50 percent of boomers play weekly, and play persists into late life with 32 percent of the Silent Generation, aged 81 to 90, playing weekly, per the ESA 2026 Essential Facts report, surveyed by YouGov among 13,545 people in February 2026.
Shape.source: ESA 2026 Essential Facts report, industry association survey with YouGov, 3 June 2026

Shape.claim: Spending concentrates in content rather than devices. Content takes about 86 percent of 2025 consumer spending, subscription spending grows 20 percent in the year, and mobile is the most used platform with 82 percent of players age 8 and older playing on a mobile device.
Shape.source: ESA annual consumer spending release, industry association

Shape.claim: Video games outpace American consumer spending on movies, television and music combined, per the ESA 2026 Essential Facts report.
Shape.source: ESA 2026 Essential Facts as reported by Game Developer, trade press

Shape.claim: The player count is the industry association's own survey. 212.3 million Americans playing weekly comes from the ESA's 2026 Essential Facts with YouGov, and each edition is that year's survey rather than a series, so quote the edition with the count and use Pew's independent teen research as the check.
Shape.source: ESA 2026 Essential Facts report, industry association survey with YouGov

Unique to this market.claim: ESRB ratings are not law. Age ratings are self-regulatory: the ESRB is an industry-established body founded in 1994, and the Supreme Court held in Brown v. Entertainment Merchants Association, 564 U.S. 786, decided 2011, that video games are protected speech under the First Amendment, striking down a state law restricting sales of violent games to minors. Enforcement runs through retailer and platform policy rather than law.
Unique to this market.card_text: Age ratings are self-regulatory, not statutory
Unique to this market.source: Supreme Court opinion via Justia, primary legal text

Unique to this market.claim: Federal consumer protection enforcement reaches games through the FTC. Epic Games agreed in December 2022 to pay 520 million dollars, a 275 million dollar penalty for children privacy violations under COPPA and 245 million dollars in refunds for dark pattern billing in Fortnite, and by June 2025 the FTC has returned nearly 200 million dollars to players.
Unique to this market.card_text: Federal enforcement runs through the FTC
Unique to this market.source: Federal Trade Commission press release, federal regulator

Unique to this market.claim: Rules for minors are being made at state level and contested in federal court. Utah enacts the first App Store Accountability Act in March 2025 requiring app stores to verify ages and obtain parental consent, Texas, Louisiana and Alabama follow with California passing a variant, a federal court enjoins the Texas law on First Amendment grounds in December 2025, and Utah amends its law in 2026 to private enforcement only with key provisions delayed to May 2027.
Unique to this market.card_text: Rules for minors are being made state by state
Unique to this market.source: Frankfurt Kurnit technology law analysis, law firm client alert

Press structure.claim: Games media ownership has consolidated into a small set of owners. Fandom acquires GameSpot and Giant Bomb in 2022, Ziff Davis IGN Entertainment acquires the Gamer Network brands including Eurogamer, GamesIndustry.biz, Rock Paper Shotgun and VG247 in 2024, and Valnet acquires Polygon in 2025.
Press structure.source: Game Developer reporting on the Polygon sale, trade press

Press structure.claim: Vox Media sells Polygon to Valnet on 1 May 2025 and the majority of its staff is laid off in the sale, including the co founder and editor in chief. Valnet is a Montreal company operating high volume aggregation sites including Screen Rant and Game Rant.
Press structure.source: Kotaku reporting, games press

Press structure.claim: Institutional homes for games journalism keep closing. The Washington Post shuts its games section Launcher and Vice shuts Waypoint in 2023, and GameStop, a games retailer, shuts Game Informer in August 2024 after 33 years before the brand is relaunched in 2025 under Gunzilla Games, a game developer.
Press structure.source: Axios reporting on the Polygon sale with sector context, national news outlet

Press structure.claim: Laid off journalists are rebuilding as owners. Aftermath launches in November 2023 as a worker owned subscription site founded by former Kotaku writers, and Fandom sells Giant Bomb to its own staff in May 2025, who run it as an independent subscriber backed operation.
Press structure.source: Game Developer reporting on the Aftermath launch, trade press

Press structure.claim: The defining pattern is ownership churn at the top and worker ownership at the edge. Legacy mastheads change hands repeatedly while subscriber funded journalist owned outlets absorb the displaced reporting capacity. This is an interpretation resting on the rows above.
Press structure.source: Game Developer and Kotaku reporting plus the rows above

Venues.claim: Do not default to X for younger American players' games talk. Among US teens the most widely used platforms are YouTube, TikTok, Snapchat and Instagram, and use of Facebook and X sits far below its level of a decade ago.
Venues.card_text: YouTube, TikTok, Snapchat and Instagram lead among teens
Venues.source: Pew Research Center, Teens and Tech topic page, independent research organisation

Venues.claim: Discord and Twitch function as the gaming community platforms for young players. Among teen gamers, 44 percent use Discord and 30 percent use Twitch, against 28 percent and 17 percent of all teens.
Venues.card_text: Discord and Twitch are the gaming-community platforms
Venues.source: Pew Research Center, Teens and Video Games Today report, independent research organisation

Venues.claim: Do not assert that Reddit, YouTube creators and podcasts are the centre of adult US games conversation without evidence. They are widely treated as such, but no citable current source establishing their scale or share was found.
Venues.source: No source meeting this directory's standard

Where the data lives.claim: ESA Essential Facts About the U.S. Video Game Industry. The industry association free annual gives player counts, demographics, platform use and attitudes, the standard first stop for who plays in America.
Where the data lives.source: Entertainment Software Association, industry association annual

Where the data lives.claim: ESA annual consumer spending release. The February release each year gives the headline US spending total with content, hardware and accessories splits, compiled with Circana and Sensor Tower, free at the top line.
Where the data lives.source: Entertainment Software Association with Circana and Sensor Tower, industry association release

Where the data lives.claim: Circana video games industry page. The vendor publishes free monthly top line US spending commentary, including monthly totals and hardware and software highlights, with the full dataset behind subscription.
Where the data lives.source: Circana, commercial data vendor, monthly

Where the data lives.claim: ESRB ratings database. The self regulator free searchable database gives any rated game age category, content descriptors, interactive elements and rating summary, and confirms whether and how a title was rated for the US market.
Where the data lives.source: Entertainment Software Rating Board, industry self regulatory body

Where the data lives.claim: FTC enforcement materials on games. The regulator case pages, refund trackers and press releases document federal action on games monetisation and children privacy, with the Epic Games matter as the anchor case.
Where the data lives.source: Federal Trade Commission, federal regulator

Where the data lives.claim: Pew Research Center teens and technology research. Free independent survey research on teen platform use and gaming habits, the corrective to industry funded demographics and the standard citation for youth venue triage.
Where the data lives.card_text: Pew Research Center, teens and tech
Where the data lives.source: Pew Research Center, independent research organisation

Where the data lives.claim: The State of Video Gaming, Matthew Ball and Epyllion. A free annual analyst presentation with market sizing, participation and platform charts for most major markets, useful for cross market comparison that no single free source provides. It aggregates many vendors rather than applying one methodology, so treat figures as the analyst assembly they are and cite the underlying source where the deck names one.
Where the data lives.card_text: The State of Video Gaming (Ball, Epyllion)
Where the data lives.source: Matthew Ball, Epyllion, independent analyst, annual presentation

known_gaps.gap: Who spends. Payer demographics and the share of spend from heavy payers are not held; the ESA gives player counts and totals, not who pays.
known_gaps.instead: Publisher filings give revenue without demographics; read any free payer figure as one vendor's panel.

known_gaps.gap: Advertising revenue. The spending figure counts content, hardware and accessories, and no source held measures mobile ad revenue.
known_gaps.instead: Say the basis with every mobile figure: in-app purchases from Sensor Tower are not the same as a total that adds advertising.

known_gaps.gap: Independent adult play surveys. The player count is the industry association's; Pew's rows are the teen series.
known_gaps.instead: Quote the ESA count as the ESA's, with the edition, and use Pew for teens only.

known_gaps.gap: Communities. The community rows for the largest market are almost all subreddits, and the profile could not verify the centrality of creator channels and podcasts.
known_gaps.instead: Use the subreddit rows for player and parent sentiment, the official-Discord technique for a title, and confirm activity by recent post dates.

player_population.source: Entertainment Software Association, 2026 Essential Facts About the U.S. Video Game Industry
player_population.definition: The figure counts Americans aged 5 to 90 who play video games for one or more hours per week, which the ESA states is 67 percent of the US population. It comes from a survey of 13,545 respondents fielded 11 to 25 February 2026.

Standing.claim: Do not size the Gulf or MENA games market from a free figure, because none meets this directory's standard. Regional revenue and player figures in circulation trace to paid vendor estimates or to promotional material produced by parties invested in the region's growth, and no free figure naming its methodology was found.
Standing.source: No source meeting this directory's standard

Standing.claim: State the border before quoting a MENA figure. Niko Partners models MENA-3, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and Egypt, and other vendors draw the region differently, with or without Turkey, Iran and Israel; this profile's sourced claims cover Saudi Arabia and the UAE. Two MENA totals that differ by billions usually differ by border, not by measurement.
Standing.source: Niko Partners MENA market page, data vendor

Market size.claim: The 23.5 million Saudi players is the strategy's own figure. Saudi Arabia, the largest national market in scope, stated a base of 23.5 million game enthusiasts, 67 percent of the population, at the launch of its National Gaming and Esports Strategy in September 2022, with no published definition of an enthusiast; ask players or payers before quoting it. No free revenue figure meeting sourcing standards exists for the market.
Market size.source: Saudi National Gaming and Esports Strategy launch coverage, Sabq, Saudi news outlet

Shape.claim: The defining structural layer is sovereign investment. Savvy Games Group, wholly owned by Saudi Arabia Public Investment Fund, completed its largest investment to date in July 2023, the 4.9 billion dollar acquisition of the mobile publisher Scopely.
Shape.source: Public Investment Fund newswire, sovereign primary disclosure

Shape.claim: Savvy Games Group also carries an announced commitment of 38 billion dollars to games from September 2022 and owns ESL FACEIT Group, and Scopely acquired the Niantic games business including Pokemon GO in 2025.
Shape.source: Naavik analysis of the Savvy portfolio, specialist games analyst

Shape.claim: The state has a published national plan for the sector. Saudi Arabia National Gaming and Esports Strategy, launched September 2022, targets 250 games companies, 39,000 jobs, a GDP contribution above 50 billion riyals, and more than 30 locally made games in the global top 300, all by 2030.
Shape.source: Government of Saudi Arabia, Vision 2030 strategy page, state primary source

Shape.claim: The demographic base is young. Saudi citizens under 35 comprise 69.4 percent of the Saudi population per 2024 data from the General Authority for Statistics, and the 2022 census puts the national median age at 29.
Shape.source: GASTAT via Saudi Press Agency, state statistics agency

Shape.claim: The region is primarily a buyer and investor rather than a producer. Domestic development capacity is an explicit build objective of the Saudi strategy rather than an existing base. The buyer and investor characterisation is an interpretation resting on the strategy targets and holdings sourced above.
Shape.source: Naavik analysis of the Savvy portfolio, specialist games analyst

Shape.claim: Do not read sovereign investment as domestic market size. Savvy Games Group's 38 billion dollar commitment and its purchases, Scopely for 4.9 billion dollars and ESL FACEIT Group, are outbound investment by the Public Investment Fund, and no free figure sizes Saudi domestic consumer spend to standard; the investment vehicle is tens of billions and the consumption market is not.
Shape.source: PIF corporate newswire, sovereign fund press releases, primary corporate disclosure

Unique to this market.claim: Game age classification in Saudi Arabia is statutory and regulator operated. The General Commission for Audiovisual Media (الهيئة العامة للإعلام المرئي والمسموع, GCAM) runs a mandatory age classification system for games in force since 15 August 2016, and the classification service is carried on the national government services portal.
Unique to this market.card_text: Saudi ratings are statutory (GCAM)
Unique to this market.source: Saudi national services portal, government primary source

Unique to this market.claim: The United Arab Emirates operates a separate statutory classification system. Age classification covering video games is binding since February 2018, introduced by the National Media Council, with games classified into age groups 3, 7, 12, 16, 18 and 21.
Unique to this market.card_text: UAE ratings are statutory
Unique to this market.source: UAE National Media Council announcement, government primary source

Unique to this market.claim: There is no single Gulf-wide games rating scheme. Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates each run their own regulator-operated binding classification, and no operating GCC-wide games rating scheme was verified, so a rating in one is not a rating in the other.
Unique to this market.card_text: No GCC-wide rating scheme
Unique to this market.source: Saudi and UAE regulator sources cited in the rows above, government primary sources

Unique to this market.claim: Government entities operate the region flagship events directly. The Esports World Cup in Riyadh carries a prize pool above 70 million dollars in 2025 across 25 tournaments, is funded by a grant from the Public Investment Fund, and is operated through ESL FACEIT Group with the Saudi Esports Federation chairing the event.
Unique to this market.card_text: The state runs the flagship events
Unique to this market.source: Esports World Cup Foundation press release, event operator

Unique to this market.claim: Regulation here moves in both directions, so date every regulatory claim. The General Commission for Audiovisual Media announced a ban on 47 games in July 2018, the cause reported at the time disputed by people in the regional industry, and the same commission now runs the statutory age classification while the state funds the Esports World Cup; anything older than a couple of years on Gulf games regulation needs checking.
Unique to this market.source: Game Developer report of the GCAM announcement, July 2018, trade press

Press structure.claim: Treat glossy English-language coverage of the Gulf games market as promotional until its funding is checked. A meaningful share of it is paid or partner content produced for state entities, including sponsored editorial hubs for the Public Investment Fund carried on international business media.
Press structure.source: Bloomberg sponsored content hub for PIF, paid partner content

Press structure.claim: Sustained analytical coverage of the Gulf games sector is produced largely from outside the region, by international esports trade press and games industry analysts.
Press structure.source: The Esports Advocate coverage of Gulf esports funding, trade press

Press structure.claim: Do not characterise the Arabic-language games press without verification. Long-running Arabic games sites exist, including سعودي جيمر (Saudi Gamer) and ترو جيمنج (True Gaming), and both show recent output, but their scale, ownership and funding could not be verified from citable sources.
Press structure.source: No source meeting this directory's standard

Venues.claim: Saudi Arabia is a platform saturated venue environment. Social media ad audiences approach the total population in early 2025, YouTube ad audience is 27.2 million, about four fifths of the population, and social media user identities skew 61.3 percent male.
Venues.card_text: Near-total platform saturation in Saudi Arabia
Venues.source: DataReportal Digital 2025 Saudi Arabia, research compilation with published methodology

Venues.claim: Do not assert a games venue hierarchy for the Gulf. Which platforms carry Arabic-language games discourse, and the balance between Arabic and English in it, could not be established from citable sources.
Venues.source: No source meeting this directory's standard

Where the data lives.claim: PIF corporate newswire. The sovereign fund own press releases are the primary record of Savvy Games Group deals and games commitments, the source of record for what has actually been announced.
Where the data lives.source: Public Investment Fund, sovereign primary disclosure

Where the data lives.claim: Vision 2030 strategy library, National Gaming and Esports Strategy page. The official statement of Saudi Arabia sector targets, the reference for what the state has committed to build and by when.
Where the data lives.source: Government of Saudi Arabia, Vision 2030 portal, state primary source

Where the data lives.claim: GASTAT, the Saudi General Authority for Statistics. Census, population and youth statistics for the region largest market, including the age structure behind every demographic claim about Saudi players.
Where the data lives.source: General Authority for Statistics, state statistics agency

Where the data lives.claim: Saudi game classification service. The government services entry for GCAM game age classification lets a researcher confirm the statutory rating regime and its administering regulator for Saudi Arabia.
Where the data lives.source: Saudi national services portal, government primary source

Where the data lives.claim: Esports World Cup Foundation press room. The operator releases give official prize pools, formats, participating clubs and titles for the region flagship event, with self reported audience figures that require independent treatment.
Where the data lives.source: Esports World Cup Foundation, state affiliated event operator

Where the data lives.claim: DataReportal country reports for Gulf states. Free annual compilations of internet and platform ad audience data with published methodology, the least interested source available for venue planning in this region.
Where the data lives.source: DataReportal, Kepios with We Are Social, research compilation, annual

Where the data lives.claim: The State of Video Gaming, Matthew Ball and Epyllion. A free annual analyst presentation with market sizing, participation and platform charts for most major markets, useful for cross market comparison that no single free source provides. It aggregates many vendors rather than applying one methodology, so treat figures as the analyst assembly they are and cite the underlying source where the deck names one.
Where the data lives.card_text: The State of Video Gaming (Ball, Epyllion)
Where the data lives.source: Matthew Ball, Epyllion, independent analyst, annual presentation

known_gaps.gap: Egypt, the Levant and the Maghreb. The profile's sourced claims cover Saudi Arabia and the UAE; the rest of the region has community rows and no claims.
known_gaps.instead: Use Niko's MENA-3 framing for Egypt with its basis named, and say the profile does not reach the Levant or North Africa.

known_gaps.gap: Market size. No free figure is held; the two data rows are Niko Partners, paid, and Power League Gaming.
known_gaps.instead: Quote a MENA figure only with its vendor, its border and its year, and treat a free number as promotional until its method is found.

known_gaps.gap: Arabic-language discourse. The Arabic press rows are unverified for scale, no Arabic channels, podcasts or newsletters are held as MENA rows, and the venue hierarchy could not be established.
known_gaps.instead: Search channels by language Arabic; read DataReportal's platform audiences from the profile card as reach, not games use.

known_gaps.gap: Turkey, Iran and Israel. Turkey is its own market tag here and Iran and Israel are not tagged, so a vendor's MENA that includes any of them will not match this profile.
known_gaps.instead: State the border with every figure and check which countries the vendor folds in.

Standing.claim: The sixth largest games market in the world by game revenue in 2023, according to a business case report prepared by Nordicity for Ukie, published 2025.
Standing.source: Nordicity report commissioned by Ukie, trade body commissioned research

Standing.claim: The world rank is a trade body's. Sixth largest by game revenue comes from a Nordicity report commissioned by Ukie, for 2023, published in 2025; quote it as Ukie's, with the year, and do not set it beside another ranker's table.
Standing.source: Nordicity report commissioned by Ukie, trade body commissioned research

Market size.claim: UK consumers spent 8.76 billion pounds on video games in 2025, up 7.4 percent year on year, per Ukie annual Consumer Games Market Valuation released in April 2026.
Market size.source: Ukie market valuation announcement, trade body annual

Shape.claim: Spending in 2025 splits into 6.03 billion pounds of software, up 7 percent, 2.17 billion pounds of hardware, up 3 percent, and 566 million pounds of game culture, up 42 percent, with digital console at 2.49 billion pounds, mobile at 2.07 billion pounds and digital PC at 1.15 billion pounds.
Shape.source: Ukie market valuation announcement, trade body annual

Shape.claim: The development workforce reached 25,419 full time equivalents in 2024, up 4.8 percent year on year.
Shape.source: TIGA data cited in the Nordicity report for Ukie, trade body sourced research

Shape.claim: The wider sector supports over 73,000 jobs and contributes 6 billion pounds in gross value added annually, and has more than doubled in size over the last decade.
Shape.source: Ukie market valuation announcement, trade body annual

Shape.claim: Do not characterise the ownership of the UK development base. Whether the largest UK studios are domestically or foreign owned could not be verified from a reliable single source.
Shape.source: No source meeting this directory's standard

Shape.claim: The Ukie headline is not software spend. Of the 8.76 billion pounds for 2025, software is 6.03 billion, hardware 2.17 billion and the game culture line 566 million. Quote the software line when you mean games and the total when you mean the valuation.
Shape.source: Ukie market valuation announcement, trade body annual

Unique to this market.claim: Age classification has statutory force. Since 30 July 2012, video games suitable only for those aged 12 and over require statutory classification before UK supply, under provisions of the Digital Economy Act 2010 brought into force with the Video Recordings (Labelling) Regulations 2012, making it an offence to supply against the labelling regime.
Unique to this market.card_text: Age ratings have statutory force
Unique to this market.source: Explanatory memorandum to SI 2012/1767, primary legal text

Unique to this market.claim: The Games Rating Authority, formerly the Video Standards Council, is the statutory body that rates video games in the UK using the PEGI system.
Unique to this market.source: Games Rating Authority official site, statutory classification body

Unique to this market.claim: Games development carries a statutory tax credit. The Video Games Expenditure Credit applies to expenditure from 1 January 2024 at a 34 percent rate, replacing Video Games Tax Relief, and qualification requires certification as British through the cultural test administered by the BFI.
Unique to this market.card_text: 34% tax credit for British-certified games
Unique to this market.source: BFI expenditure credits guidance, arm length public body administrator

Unique to this market.claim: Loot boxes are not regulated by law in the UK. The government's July 2022 response to its call for evidence found an association between loot boxes and harms, declined to legislate, and set an industry-led approach with a technical working group convened by DCMS, holding legislation in reserve.
Unique to this market.card_text: Loot boxes are not regulated in law
Unique to this market.source: UK government response, primary policy document

Unique to this market.claim: The industry answer to the loot box decision is a published code. Ukie issued 11 industry principles on loot boxes in July 2023, developed by the DCMS convened technical working group, covering parental consent expectations, spending controls and transparency.
Unique to this market.source: Ukie principles announcement, trade body

Unique to this market.claim: The rater changed its name. The Video Standards Council became the Games Rating Authority on 2 June 2023, so a source naming the VSC Rating Board is describing the same statutory body under its old name. Its statutory role covers boxed games; digital storefronts use IARC.
Unique to this market.source: VSC announcement of the renaming, via Games Press, industry press-release wire

Press structure.claim: The UK legacy specialist publishing stable changed hands to an American buyer. IGN Entertainment acquired Gamer Network, whose brands include Eurogamer, GamesIndustry.biz, Rock Paper Shotgun and VG247, from ReedPop in 2024, and the period since has included multiple rounds of redundancies and the departure of key editorial staff.
Press structure.source: The Game Business reporting, specialist trade outlet

Press structure.claim: Digital Foundry, the technical analysis brand part owned by IGN through the Gamer Network acquisition, bought its way to full independence in August 2025, with its owner citing the volatile games media landscape and a belief in independent specialists.
Press structure.source: The Game Business reporting, specialist trade outlet
