Press structure.claim: The largest remaining UK owned games media brands sit inside one listed company. PC Gamer, Edge and GamesRadar+ are Future brands, and Future is listed on the London Stock Exchange.
Press structure.source: Future plc corporate site, primary corporate disclosure

Press structure.claim: A subscriber funded independent trade layer has formed around displaced senior journalists. The Game Business is an independent outlet covering the business of games founded by Christopher Dring, previously head of GamesIndustry.biz.
Press structure.source: The Game Business, the outlet own reporting with author disclosure

Press structure.claim: The UK pattern is absorption of the legacy stable by an overseas consolidator, one large domestic listed owner holding the remaining major brands, and senior veterans rebuilding as independents. This is an interpretation resting on the rows above.
Press structure.source: The Game Business reporting plus the rows above, specialist trade outlet

Venues.claim: The audience base for venue planning is broad. Ofcom research found 60 percent of UK adults, and 88 percent of those aged 16 to 24, played games on an electronic device in 2021.
Venues.source: Ofcom research as cited in the DCMS government response, government document

Venues.claim: Do not assert a UK venue hierarchy. Which platforms carry UK games conversation, and in what proportion, could not be established from a citable UK-specific source.
Venues.source: No source meeting this directory's standard

Where the data lives.claim: Ukie Consumer Games Market Valuation. The trade body annual valuation gives total UK consumer spend with software, hardware and game culture splits, released free each spring, the standard headline sizing for the UK market.
Where the data lives.source: Ukie, trade body annual

Where the data lives.claim: Ukiepedia. The trade body open wiki of UK industry statistics collects valuation history, headline industry facts and global market context in one navigable place, with revision methodology stated.
Where the data lives.source: Ukie, trade body reference wiki

Where the data lives.claim: Games Rating Authority ratings search. The statutory classifier searchable database confirms any game UK age rating and content information, and carries annual reports on classification activity.
Where the data lives.source: Games Rating Authority, statutory classification body

Where the data lives.claim: BFI certification and expenditure credit guidance. The administrator pages give the rules, rates and cultural test criteria for the Video Games Expenditure Credit, the reference for how UK games production is subsidised.
Where the data lives.source: British Film Institute, arm length public body

Where the data lives.claim: DCMS Economic Estimates. Accredited official statistics on gross value added for DCMS sectors, including computer games subsector estimates, the independent government check on trade body economic claims.
Where the data lives.source: Department for Culture, Media and Sport, accredited official statistics

Where the data lives.claim: legislation.gov.uk. The official statute database holds the primary texts of the games classification regime and every other UK law a games researcher needs to cite, the citation of record over any summary.
Where the data lives.source: The National Archives, official legislation database

Where the data lives.claim: The State of Video Gaming, Matthew Ball and Epyllion. A free annual analyst presentation with market sizing, participation and platform charts for most major markets, useful for cross market comparison that no single free source provides. It aggregates many vendors rather than applying one methodology, so treat figures as the analyst assembly they are and cite the underlying source where the deck names one.
Where the data lives.card_text: The State of Video Gaming (Ball, Epyllion)
Where the data lives.source: Matthew Ball, Epyllion, independent analyst, annual presentation

Where the data lives.claim: The weekly UK chart is not the UK market. GSD, run by Sparkers, covers physical sales plus the digital sales of participating publishers, and Nintendo does not participate in digital, so Switch digital is a hole; mobile is outside the chart altogether.
Where the data lives.source: Sparkers GSD, per the directory's Sparkers row, data vendor

known_gaps.gap: Communities. No UK community row is held, and the profile could not establish which platforms carry UK games conversation.
known_gaps.instead: Use the games-specific subreddit and official-Discord techniques; the UK's English-language discourse mixes with the US's, so a venue found is rarely UK-only.

known_gaps.gap: Current play participation. The profile's 60 percent of adults is Ofcom's 2021 figure, and no later UK play figure is held.
known_gaps.instead: Ofcom's Online Nation and children's media series are the rows to check for a newer edition; quote the year with the figure.

known_gaps.gap: Workforce reconciliation. Headcount comes from TIGA, Ukie's census and DCMS on three definitions, and no reconciliation is held.
known_gaps.instead: Cite one series with its definition and year, and record the spread between them as a finding rather than an error.

known_gaps.gap: Boxed retail chart. The weekly physical chart is not held as a row; the directory's UK sales data is GSD via Sparkers and Ampere.
known_gaps.instead: Treat the trade-press weekly chart as GSD's, with its participating-publisher digital coverage, and say so.

player_population.definition: 38 million is a rough estimate derived from Statista, a paid data aggregator. No UK body publishes a player headcount on a stated method. Ofcom last measured participation in 2021, at 60 percent of adults aged 16 and over, and gives no headcount. Ukie publishes the consumer market value rather than player numbers.

Standing.claim: Do not look for a French world rank in the trade body's data, because SELL states none. It describes video games as the country's first cultural and creative industry by revenue, a standing among French cultural industries rather than a rank among games markets. A rank comes from an analyst, on that analyst's basis.
Standing.source: SELL market results as reported by AFJV, trade press

Market size.claim: The French games market reaches 5.856 billion euros in 2025, up 2.9 percent year on year and its second highest level on record, per SELL annual market report.
Market size.source: SELL market results as reported by AFJV, trade press

Market size.claim: The 5.856 billion euros is the publishers' body's assembly from named panels. SELL uses GSD for physical sales, GSD and Ipsos GameTrack for digital, Sensor Tower and GameTrack for mobile and IDC for hardware. In 2025 a GameTrack methodology change moved the perimeter of on-demand services, MMO subscriptions, free-to-play MMO, social and browser games and subscriptions, and 2024 hardware history was revised, so take earlier years from the April 2026 edition rather than from an older one.
Market size.source: SELL, L'Essentiel du Jeu Video, Bilan du marche francais 2025, April 2026, trade body publication

Shape.claim: Consumer spending splits across three ecosystems in 2025. Console leads with 44 percent of the market at 2.552 billion euros, mobile takes 30 percent at 1.792 billion euros growing 11 percent, and PC gaming holds 26 percent at 1.512 billion euros.
Shape.source: SELL market results as reported by AFJV, trade press

Shape.claim: 40.2 million French people play video games in 2025, more than seven in ten, with adults making up 88 percent of players, an average age of 40, and a near even split of 51 percent men and 49 percent women.
Shape.source: SELL and Mediametrie, Les Francais et le Jeu Video 2025, as reported by AFJV, trade press

Shape.claim: Play is regular rather than occasional. 76 percent of players play at least weekly in 2025, and regular players average 7 hours 55 minutes per week, 38 minutes more than in 2024.
Shape.source: SELL and Mediametrie study as reported by ConsoleFun, games site

Shape.claim: The development sector is surveyed annually on a verified base. The SNJV 2024 barometer covers 575 verified development companies, and reports women at 20 percent of studio staff, down four points from 2022, and 14.2 percent of leadership roles.
Shape.source: SNJV Barometre annuel du jeu video 2024, trade body sector census

Shape.claim: The player count is the publishers' body's own study. 40.2 million players comes from the SELL and Mediametrie survey of 4,001 people aged 10 to 80, run online from 19 June to 13 July 2025; quote it as SELL's with Mediametrie, with the year, and do not set it beside another country's count, which will define a player differently.
Shape.source: SELL and Mediametrie, Les Francais et le Jeu Video 2025, as printed in the April 2026 Bilan, trade body survey

Unique to this market.claim: Games production carries a cultural tax credit. The credit d impot jeu video covers 30 percent of eligible production spending, capped at 6 million euros per company per financial year, with eligibility resting on a cultural scale called the bareme Contribution au developpement de la creation.
Unique to this market.card_text: 30% production tax credit
Unique to this market.source: Ministry of the Economy guidance, government primary source

Unique to this market.claim: The credit is gated by the CNC. A provisional agrement is granted by the Centre national du cinema et de l image animee after selection by an expert committee, and a definitive agrement after completion confirms the game met the required conditions.
Unique to this market.card_text: The film institution gates games funding
Unique to this market.source: Centre national du cinema et de l image animee, public cultural agency

Unique to this market.claim: The official French games terminology binds officials, not you. Terms published through the language enrichment process, including jeu video de competition for e-sport and joueur-animateur en direct for streamer, are required of government bodies and officials, not of the public, the press or companies, so their force is narrower than commonly reported.
Unique to this market.card_text: Official games terminology binds the state only
Unique to this market.source: BBC reporting on the official terminology, international news outlet

Unique to this market.claim: France runs a live experiment regulating web3 games. Articles 40 and 41 of law 2024-449 of 21 May 2024, the loi SREN, create a three year experimental framework for jeux a objets numeriques monetisables (JONUM, games with monetisable digital objects), regulated by the Autorite nationale des jeux, with the implementing decree in force since 7 February 2026.
Unique to this market.card_text: JONUM, a three year web3 games experiment
Unique to this market.source: Autorite nationale des jeux, regulator JONUM page, state authority

Unique to this market.claim: Physical game sales hold up better in France than in neighbouring markets. Physical console game sales fell 12 percent in 2025, or 4 percent counting games bundled with consoles, and SELL attributes the resilience to a strong and unique retail network and a durable consumer attachment to physical media.
Unique to this market.card_text: Physical retail is unusually resilient
Unique to this market.source: SELL market results as reported by AFJV, trade press

Unique to this market.claim: PEGI is not voluntary in France. Homologated by the Ministry of the Interior since 2015, the PEGI classification is required for any game distributed in France, and PEGI in France is administered by SELL's delegue general, so the publishers' body runs the rating it reports on.
Unique to this market.source: AFJV report on PEGI classification in France, 10 December 2018, trade press

Press structure.claim: The consumer games media market is led by Webedia through jeuxvideo.com, with Reworld Media building the number two position through serial acquisitions including the Melty gaming brands, Eclypsia, JeuVideo-Live and the Unify portfolio.
Press structure.source: AFP reporting via Frenchweb, business news outlet

Press structure.claim: The scale of the leading group is measured independently. Webedia properties reach 28.6 million monthly unique visitors in France in May 2025, per Mediametrie internet audience ranking.
Press structure.source: Mediametrie audience data as reported by La Reclame, advertising trade press

Press structure.claim: The defining press event is a newsroom exodus. TF1 sold its Unify digital division including Gamekult to Reworld Media in 2022, and nearly the entire Gamekult editorial team resigned in November 2022 through the clause de cession, citing a hostile context for press independence.
Press structure.source: Jeuxvideo.com news reporting, games press

Press structure.claim: Do not characterise the independent French games press. Whether a significant independent or subscriber-funded layer remains at scale, around titles such as Canard PC, could not be verified from citable sources.
Press structure.source: No source meeting this directory's standard

Press structure.claim: The French pattern is concentration under two horizontal digital media groups, with newsroom exodus as the recurring response. This is an interpretation resting on the ownership rows above.
Press structure.source: AFP reporting via Frenchweb plus the rows above, business news outlet

Venues.claim: Play runs through a smartphone and console pairing. Players combine 2.2 platforms on average in 2025, with the smartphone used by 59 percent of players and the console by 58 percent, and the console used by three quarters of players aged 10 to 30.
Venues.card_text: Smartphone and console, 2.2 platforms per player
Venues.source: SELL and Mediametrie study as reported by AFJV, trade press

Venues.claim: Live streaming reaches mass audience scale in France. Mediametrie annual internet review records a Twitch peak of 2.5 million unique visitors on 5 October 2025 during GP Explorer, an event organised by the content creator Squeezie.
Venues.source: Mediametrie, The Internet Year 2025, audience measurement body

Venues.claim: Do not assert a French venue hierarchy. The relative weight of YouTube games content, Discord, jeuxvideo.com forums and other spaces could not be sourced: the SELL and Mediametrie 2025 study covers play practice, devices and motivations but publishes no venue shares, and Mediametrie's Internet Year 2025 ranks sites and groups without splitting games conversation by platform.
Venues.source: Sources checked and found not to contain the needed data, documented gap

Where the data lives.claim: SELL, L Essentiel du Jeu Video. The trade body twice yearly publication gives market sizing with named data panels in spring and the player study in autumn, free, the standard reference for the French consumer market.
Where the data lives.source: SELL, trade body publication series

Where the data lives.claim: Les Francais et le Jeu Video, SELL with Mediametrie. The annual player study gives player counts, demographics, devices, frequency and spending with a documented representative methodology, the reference for who plays in France.
Where the data lives.card_text: Les Français et le Jeu Vidéo
Where the data lives.source: SELL and Mediametrie, annual survey publication

Where the data lives.claim: SNJV sector publications. The development trade body publishes the annual Barometre du jeu video, a census of French development companies, and monthly employment data, the production side complement to SELL consumer data.
Where the data lives.source: SNJV, trade body sector census and employment series

Where the data lives.claim: CNC games funding pages. The public cultural agency pages give the rules and process for the credit d impot jeu video and its selective games aid, the reference for how French games production is publicly financed.
Where the data lives.source: Centre national du cinema et de l image animee, public cultural agency

Where the data lives.claim: ANJ JONUM pages. The gambling regulator pages carry the legal framework, decrees and the list of declared operators for the experimental web3 games regime, the primary record of the fastest moving regulation in this market.
Where the data lives.source: Autorite nationale des jeux, state regulator

Where the data lives.claim: Mediametrie internet audience publications. The audience measurement body free releases give monthly and annual internet audience for France at site and group level with documented methodology, the independent check on any French platform or media scale claim.
Where the data lives.source: Mediametrie, audience measurement body

Where the data lives.claim: The State of Video Gaming, Matthew Ball and Epyllion. A free annual analyst presentation with market sizing, participation and platform charts for most major markets, useful for cross market comparison that no single free source provides. It aggregates many vendors rather than applying one methodology, so treat figures as the analyst assembly they are and cite the underlying source where the deck names one.
Where the data lives.card_text: The State of Video Gaming (Ball, Epyllion)
Where the data lives.source: Matthew Ball, Epyllion, independent analyst, annual presentation

known_gaps.instead: Channels are found by language French rather than by market; podcasts and newsletters are not held at all.

known_gaps.gap: Mobile publishers. The French mobile publishing layer, hypercasual and browser-era publishers included, has no rows.
known_gaps.instead: Publisher filings for the listed ones and the Global Sensor Tower rows are the route; say the directory does not hold the layer.

known_gaps.gap: Streaming and esports. The profile carries Twitch's French peak from Mediametrie but no French streamer, esports organisation or event rows.
known_gaps.instead: Treat the Mediametrie figure as the only sourced scale here, and open an organisation's own site for anything else.

known_gaps.gap: Communities and people. One community row, r/jeuxvideo, and one people row for the whole market, and the profile could not rank venues.

player_population.source: SELL and Médiamétrie, L'Essentiel du Jeu Vidéo, April 2026
player_population.definition: The figure counts people in France aged 10 to 80 who played a video game at least once in the year. SELL states 76 percent of them play at least weekly and 24 percent play occasionally. The data comes from Médiamétrie, an online survey of 4,001 individuals representative of the French population aged 10 to 80, with fieldwork from 19 June to 13 July 2025.

Standing.claim: Do not look for an Italian world rank in the trade body's data, because IIDEA states none. Its annual report describes video games as among the most loved entertainment forms of Italians and presents domestic figures without ranking Italy among games markets. A rank comes from an analyst, on that analyst's basis.
Standing.source: IIDEA annual report press release, trade body

Market size.claim: Italian consumer spending on video games is about 2.4 billion euros in 2025, down 1 percent year on year, per IIDEA's annual report I videogiochi in Italia nel 2025, produced by Ipsos for the association and presented at the Ministry of Enterprises and Made in Italy in Rome on 13 May 2026. The 2024 edition had put it at nearly 2.4 billion, up 3 percent.
Market size.source: IIDEA annual report press release, 13 May 2026, trade body

Market size.claim: The Italian market figure is the trade body's research, run by Ipsos. IIDEA commissions its annual I videogiochi in Italia from Ipsos and presents it at a ministry each spring; quote it as IIDEA's with Ipsos, with the year, and do not set its 2.4 billion euros beside a vendor's Italy estimate without naming both bases.
Market size.source: IIDEA annual report press release, 13 May 2026, trade body

Shape.claim: Spending concentrates in software. Software is about 1.8 billion euros in 2025, down 1 percent and 77 percent of the total; smartphone games take 929 million euros, and among console and PC games digital is 59 percent at 328 million euros against 41 percent physical at 231 million; consoles grow 3 percent to about 400 million euros and accessories fall 5 percent to 152 million.
Shape.source: IIDEA annual report press release, 13 May 2026, trade body

Shape.claim: 14.2 million people in Italy play video games in 2025, stable on the previous year, 60 percent men and 40 percent women, about 60 percent under 35, playing 7 hours 53 minutes a week on average and up to 15 hours among 12 to 17 year olds.
Shape.source: IIDEA annual report press release, 13 May 2026, trade body

Shape.claim: The production sector is small relative to consumption. Italian games companies number 200, up 25 percent over two years, employ 2,800 people, up 17 percent, and generate estimated revenue between 180 and 200 million euros, up 36 percent since 2022.
Shape.source: IIDEA annual report press release, trade body

Shape.claim: Italian studios build for export and fund themselves. Europe takes 42 percent of the destination market for Italian published games and North America 37 percent, while Italy takes 12 percent, and 88 percent of studios rely on self financing.
Shape.source: IIDEA annual report press release, trade body

Shape.claim: IIDEA's report lands each spring for the previous year, so quote the edition with the figure. The edition for 2025 was presented on 13 May 2026, and this profile's 2025 figures are that edition's; the studio census figures still carry the earlier edition, which the 2025 release does not restate.
Shape.source: IIDEA annual report press release, 13 May 2026, trade body

Unique to this market.claim: Games production carries a statutory cultural tax credit. The credito d imposta for the production of video games of Italian nationality with cultural value rests on article 15 of law 220 of 2016, the cinema law, and ministerial decree 187 of 12 May 2021, and is administered by the Direzione generale Cinema e audiovisivo of the Ministry of Culture, which publishes beneficiary decrees.
Unique to this market.card_text: Games funding runs through the cinema law
Unique to this market.source: Ministry of Culture, DGCA tax credit notices index, government primary source

Unique to this market.claim: Italian classification is mandatory, but sale is not restricted. An AGCOM regulation from 2019 introduced for the first time an obligation to classify video games distributed in Italy, recognising PEGI with an AGCOM scheme for unrated titles, and selling an 18-rated game to a minor is not an offence, because the obligation is to classify, not to restrict sale.
Unique to this market.card_text: Ratings are mandatory, sales are not restricted
Unique to this market.source: AESVI clarification as reported by Tom s Hardware Italia, tech outlet

Press structure.claim: The largest games outlet is domestically owned and founder led. Multiplayer.it is operated by NetAddiction srl of Terni, founded by Andrea Pucci, and the publisher reports over 3 million monthly unique users for the site.
Press structure.source: NetAddiction corporate news page, company self description

Press structure.claim: NetAddiction is a diversified domestic digital publisher rather than a games only company, controlling Multiplayer.it, Movieplayer.it, Dissapore.com and LegaNerd.com among others, and sold its Multiplayer.com ecommerce operation to the distributor Cidiverte to refocus on editorial and advertising services.
Press structure.source: Engage, advertising trade press

Press structure.claim: International brands have retreated. Eurogamer Italia suspended publication on 4 November 2022, with its farewell note citing changed times and financial constraints.
Press structure.source: GamerClick reporting quoting the farewell note, games site

Press structure.claim: Do not call the Italian consumer games press unusually healthy, or unusually weak. One large domestically owned outlet with a self-reported multi-million audience and named editorial staff is verified, as is the closure of an international brand's Italian edition in 2022, but the wider picture could not be established either way.
Press structure.source: Assessment against the sourced rows above, no single source

Press structure.claim: Search under the old name for anything before 2020. The trade body was AESVI until February 2020, when it became IIDEA, Italian Interactive Digital Entertainment Association, so earlier market reports, censuses and coverage sit under AESVI and a search on IIDEA alone cuts the history off.
Press structure.source: Everyeye report of the renaming, games press

Venues.claim: Mobile leads device use. 11.1 million Italian players use a smartphone in 2025, followed by 6.5 million on console and 3.7 million on PC.
Venues.card_text: Mobile leads, then console, then PC
Venues.source: IIDEA annual report press release, 13 May 2026, trade body

Venues.claim: The venue planning base is broad. Italy total digital audience is 43.99 million monthly users in September 2025, 75.4 percent of the population aged 2 to 74, measured across smartphone, tablet and computer by the Audiweb system distributed by Audicom.
Venues.source: Audicom, Audiweb total digital audience release, industry measurement body

Venues.claim: The one venue hierarchy datum available places Twitch first. The publisher of Multiplayer.it cites Comscore data ranking gaming information sites in Italy with Twitch first and Multiplayer.it second in the category in 2023.
Venues.source: NetAddiction corporate news page citing Comscore, company self description

Venues.claim: Do not assert an Italian venue hierarchy beyond one datum. Audicom's free monthly communiques for May, June and September 2025 publish category audiences for news, sport, government and broadcasters and break out no games category, with per-brand data behind registration, and IIDEA's report publishes no venue shares; the one available figure is a publisher-cited Comscore ranking with Twitch first.
Venues.source: Sources checked and found not to contain the needed data, documented gap

Where the data lives.claim: IIDEA annual report, I videogiochi in Italia. The trade body free annual gives market value, player demographics and an industry census of Italian companies, presented each spring, the standard reference for the Italian market.
Where the data lives.source: IIDEA, trade body annual

Where the data lives.claim: Ministry of Culture DGCA tax credit notices. The permanent notices index carries every session opening and beneficiary decree for the games tax credit, letting a researcher see which Italian studios and games receive public production support and when.
Where the data lives.card_text: Ministry of Culture tax credit notices
Where the data lives.source: Direzione generale Cinema e audiovisivo, government body

Where the data lives.claim: Audicom, the Audiweb system. Italy joint industry internet audience measurement publishes free monthly communiques with total and category level digital audience, with per brand data available behind registration, the independent check on any Italian site or platform scale claim.
Where the data lives.source: Audicom, industry measurement body

Where the data lives.claim: Digital Bros financial reports. The Milan listed parent of 505 Games publishes full annual and interim reports with revenue split across premium games, free to play and Italian distribution, primary disclosure from Italy largest listed games company.
Where the data lives.source: Digital Bros S.p.A., primary corporate disclosure

Where the data lives.claim: The State of Video Gaming, Matthew Ball and Epyllion. A free annual analyst presentation with market sizing, participation and platform charts for most major markets, useful for cross market comparison that no single free source provides. It aggregates many vendors rather than applying one methodology, so treat figures as the analyst assembly they are and cite the underlying source where the deck names one.
Where the data lives.card_text: The State of Video Gaming (Ball, Epyllion)
Where the data lives.source: Matthew Ball, Epyllion, independent analyst, annual presentation

known_gaps.gap: Public funding beneficiaries. No row for Invitalia's First Playable Fund or the tax-credit beneficiary lists; the Ministry of Culture notices are a profile card only.
known_gaps.instead: Open the DGCA notices from the profile card and read announced budgets and paid-out lists as different figures.

known_gaps.gap: Company filings. No route to Italian company accounts is held, and Digital Bros is a profile card rather than a row.
known_gaps.instead: Read a studio count as a census figure, not a set of accounts, and open the Digital Bros reports from the card for the one audited series.

known_gaps.gap: People and communities. No Italian people rows, two subreddits and three podcasts for the whole market, and the profile could not rank venues beyond one Comscore datum.
known_gaps.instead: Use the games-specific subreddit technique, r/italygames not r/italy, and the outlets' own comment sections; treat any venue share as unsourced.

known_gaps.gap: Physical retail and platform mix. The profile carries device use by player counts but no sales-by-channel or platform-share figure.
known_gaps.instead: GSD via Sparkers is the held sales panel for Italy; say which panel a platform share comes from.

player_population.source: IIDEA, I Videogiochi in Italia nel 2025
player_population.definition: The figure counts people in Italy aged 6 to 75 who played a video game or game app on any device at least once in the previous 12 months, including occasional play, which IIDEA states is 29 percent of that age group. The data comes from the Ipsos GameTrack panel, with fieldwork in January and February 2026 among about 3,000 online respondents.

Standing.claim: Do not look for a Canadian world rank in the trade body's data, because ESAC states none. Its 2024 industry report release describes Canada as a global leader in video game development without ranking the sector or the consumer market. A rank comes from an analyst, on that analyst's basis.
Standing.source: ESAC industry report release via CNW, trade body

Market size.claim: There is no free Canadian consumer-spend figure to standard, so the anchor here sizes the industry. The video game industry contributes 5.1 billion dollars to Canada's GDP in 2024, up 3 percent since 2021, per an economic impact study by Nordicity for ESAC; that is production, not what Canadians spend.
Market size.source: ESAC and Nordicity industry report release via CNW, trade body commissioned study

Market size.claim: ESAC's figures are Canadian dollars and the study compares three years apart. The 5.1 billion dollar GDP contribution, 821 studios, 34,010 full-time equivalents and 102,000 dollar average salary come from Nordicity's study for ESAC released on 28 January 2025, and its changes are against 2021, not the previous year, so a year-on-year does not exist and a US-dollar conversion moves every figure by the exchange rate.
Market size.source: ESAC and Nordicity industry report release via CNW, 28 January 2025, trade body commissioned study

Shape.claim: The production sector is large and well paid. Canada has 821 active studios employing 34,010 full time equivalents in 2024 at an average salary of 102,000 dollars, with 86 percent full time and an average age of 34.
Shape.source: ESAC and Nordicity industry report release via CNW, trade body commissioned study

Shape.claim: Production is export facing. 88 percent of the industry revenue comes from exports.
Shape.source: ESAC and Nordicity industry report release via CNW, trade body commissioned study

Shape.claim: Employment concentrates in three provinces. Quebec has 15,220 games industry employees, British Columbia 10,930 and Ontario 6,090, together about 94 percent of the national total.
Shape.source: ESAC and Nordicity industry report release via CNW, trade body commissioned study

Shape.claim: Ownership by count skews domestic in Quebec. The Guilde du jeu video du Quebec states that Quebec studios are 86 percent Quebec owned.
Shape.source: Guilde du jeu video du Quebec communique as reproduced by Le Beta-Testeur, games site

Shape.claim: Around 20 million Canadians play video games as of 2025, spending roughly eight hours per week playing.
Shape.source: Canada Media Fund Perspectives analysis, public private funding body research

Shape.claim: Two Canadian player counts circulate, so say whose. ESAC's own site says 23 million Canadians are gamers; the Canada Media Fund's synthesis says around 20 million as of 2025, playing roughly eight hours a week. Neither page states its definition of a player, so quote one with its source and do not read the gap as growth.
Shape.source: ESAC site, trade body, as read 8 Sep 2026

Unique to this market.claim: Quebec games credit is generous and shrinking on a published schedule. The credit d impot pour la production de titres multimedias, which cost Quebec 409 million dollars in 2023 at a maximum refundable rate of 37.5 percent on salaries, is being reshaped from the March 2024 budget, with the refundable portion falling to 27.5 percent by 2028 and a new 10 percent non refundable portion payable only against Quebec tax.
Unique to this market.card_text: Quebec is cutting its credit through 2028
Unique to this market.source: La Presse reporting on the 2024 Quebec budget, national daily

Unique to this market.claim: Quebec second relevant credit is also being reshaped. The credit d impot pour le developpement des affaires electroniques pays 30 percent on eligible salaries, with significant calculation changes applying to financial years beginning after 31 December 2024 including replacement of the salary cap by an annual exclusion threshold.
Unique to this market.source: Investissement Quebec CDAE information sheet, provincial agency primary source

Unique to this market.claim: Ontario credit rewards owning the product. The Ontario Interactive Digital Media Tax Credit pays 40 percent on eligible Ontario labour plus marketing and distribution costs for products a company develops and markets itself, and 35 percent for fee for service work and for qualifying digital game corporations.
Unique to this market.card_text: Ontario pays more if you own the product
Unique to this market.source: Ontario Creates OIDMTC page, provincial agency primary source

Unique to this market.claim: British Columbia raised its credit. The interactive digital media tax credit pays 25 percent of eligible salary and wages incurred after 31 August 2025, up from 17.5 percent before that date.
Unique to this market.card_text: British Columbia raised its credit to 25%
Unique to this market.source: Government of British Columbia IDMTC page, provincial primary source

Unique to this market.claim: ESRB ratings carry Canadian legal force in some provinces. Peer-reviewed analysis records that provincial statutes in Ontario, Manitoba, New Brunswick, Nova Scotia and Saskatchewan enforce the ESRB age restrictions on the sale and rental of games, a United States industry system given statutory effect province by province, so do not assume the US self-regulatory model travels north unchanged.
Unique to this market.card_text: A US rating system with Canadian legal force
Unique to this market.source: Canadian Journal of Communication, peer reviewed article

Press structure.claim: A dedicated Canadian consumer games press exists. CGMagazine, published by CGMagazine Publishing Inc. of St. Catharines, Ontario, is a Canadian print and digital games and comics publication founded in 2010, with named editorial staff and issues published through the end of 2025.
Press structure.source: CGMagazine corporate release via CNW, publisher own release on the official wire

Press structure.claim: Canadian general interest technology media cover games as a regular beat, with MobileSyrup detailed reporting on the ESAC industry report, including an interview with the association chief executive, as a verified example.
Press structure.source: MobileSyrup reporting, Canadian technology outlet

Venues.claim: Playtime concentrates in the youngest players. Canadian players aged 13 to 17 spend the most time playing, with boys averaging 11.5 hours and girls 7.3 hours per week.
Venues.source: Canada Media Fund Perspectives analysis citing ESAC data, funding body research

Venues.claim: Games conversation runs substantially inside play itself. In ESAC 2022 player survey, 67 percent of Canadian players say games can introduce them to new friends and relationships, 48 percent spent time with people they would not have otherwise, and 38 percent met a good friend or spouse through games.
Venues.source: ESAC Essential Facts 2022 release, trade body survey by NPD Group

Venues.claim: Do not assert a Canadian venue hierarchy. The platform hierarchy of Canadian games conversation could not be sourced: ESAC's Essential Facts 2022 release covers social play but publishes no platform venue shares, the Canada Media Fund synthesis covers playtime by demographic but not venues, and Statistics Canada's cultural indicators do not break out games conversation.
Venues.source: Sources checked and found not to contain the needed data, documented gap

Where the data lives.claim: ESAC industry reports. The trade body Nordicity conducted economic studies give studio counts, employment by province, salaries, GDP contribution and export share for the production sector, the standard reference on Canada as a maker of games.
Where the data lives.source: ESAC with Nordicity, trade body commissioned series

Where the data lives.claim: ESAC player research. The trade body player survey series gives Canadian player counts, demographics, habits and attitudes.
Where the data lives.source: ESAC, trade body player survey series

Where the data lives.claim: Ontario Creates OIDMTC pages. The provincial agency pages give the credit rules, rates and eligibility tracks, and its certification role makes it the reference point for Ontario games production support.
Where the data lives.source: Ontario Creates, provincial agency

Where the data lives.claim: British Columbia IDMTC page. The province tax page states the current credit rate and eligibility for interactive digital media, the primary record for British Columbia games production support.
Where the data lives.source: Government of British Columbia, provincial primary source

Where the data lives.claim: Investissement Quebec tax measure sheets. The agency fiches detaillees state the terms of Quebec credits including the CDAE, in French, the primary reference for the province at the centre of Canadian games production.
Where the data lives.source: Investissement Quebec, provincial agency primary source

Where the data lives.claim: Canada Media Fund research and Perspectives. The public private fund publishes free games relevant research syntheses with footnoted sources, and its funding programs reach interactive digital media, a federal complement to provincial production data.
Where the data lives.source: Canada Media Fund, public private funding body

Where the data lives.claim: The State of Video Gaming, Matthew Ball and Epyllion. A free annual analyst presentation with market sizing, participation and platform charts for most major markets, useful for cross market comparison that no single free source provides. It aggregates many vendors rather than applying one methodology, so treat figures as the analyst assembly they are and cite the underlying source where the deck names one.
Where the data lives.card_text: The State of Video Gaming (Ball, Epyllion)
Where the data lives.source: Matthew Ball, Epyllion, independent analyst, annual presentation

known_gaps.gap: Consumer spend. No free Canadian consumer-spend figure is held to standard; the one data row, Circana, is US-centric.
known_gaps.instead: Size the industry from ESAC and say so, or take a vendor's Canada estimate with its basis named; do not extrapolate from a US ratio without saying you did.

known_gaps.gap: Communities and media. No community rows and no Canadian channels, podcasts or newsletters are held as CA rows.
known_gaps.instead: Use the games-specific subreddit and official-Discord techniques; the English-language discourse mixes with the US's, and the French-language layer needs French search.

known_gaps.gap: Ownership of the big studios. The profile states Quebec studios are 86 percent Quebec-owned by count and nothing on who owns the largest employers.
known_gaps.instead: Publisher filings, held for the foreign parents, give country headcount; read a Canadian studio's name as a location until its owner is checked.

known_gaps.gap: Provincial data beyond Quebec and Ontario. Interactive Ontario and the Guilde are held; no British Columbia or Atlantic association row.
known_gaps.instead: Read the ESAC provincial split as the only national series and the province's own tax page for BC.

player_population.definition: About 23 million Canadians – roughly 61% of the country’s population – identify as gamers.

Standing.claim: Do not quote Brazil's world rank from a Brazilian source without the ranker, the basis and the year, because every rank in them relays Newzoo and the relays disagree. Abragames' 2022 industry survey calls Brazil the largest games market in Latin America and tenth in the world by revenue, citing Newzoo for 2021; Fast Company Brasil gave twelfth in August 2022, also citing Newzoo; and Abragames' 2023 survey calls Brazil fifth by online population, with an estimated 103 million players. A rank comes from Newzoo's own release, on Newzoo's basis, with its year.
Standing.source: Abragames and ApexBrasil, Pesquisa da Indústria Brasileira de Games 2022, by Homo Ludens, trade body survey

Standing.claim: Do not size the Brazilian consumer market from the 13 billion reais a year in circulation, because no source for it names a publisher, a year or a method. It ran unsourced in Forbes Brasil in October 2022, in CartaCapital in September 2023 and in Diário do Comércio in July 2025, and no Abragames survey, fact sheet or white paper opened for this scan states it. Relays of Newzoo differ too: more than 2.3 billion dollars for 2021 in Abragames' 2022 fact sheet, 2.7 billion dollars for 2021 in IstoÉ Dinheiro and 2.7 billion dollars for 2022 in CartaCapital. Take a consumer figure from the analyst's own release, in its currency, with its basis and year.

Market size.claim: There is no free Brazilian consumer-spend figure to standard, so the anchor here sizes the development industry. Brazilian games studios had an estimated revenue of 251.6 million US dollars in 2022, per the 2023 Brazilian Gaming Industry Survey that GA Consulting conducted for Abragames and ApexBrasil's Brazil Games project; that is what Brazilian studios earn, not what Brazilians spend, and the survey puts it at only 10 percent of Brazilian players' consumption.
Market size.source: Abragames and ApexBrasil, 2023 Brazilian Gaming Industry Survey by GA Consulting, trade body survey

Market size.claim: The studio revenue is a model whose basis changed in the 2023 edition, so it makes no growth rate with earlier years. The survey takes each respondent's revenue band at its lower value, replaces the exporters' figures with their reported exports in dollars, converts the rest at an average 5.16 reais to the dollar and adds the AppMagic-tracked revenue of studios that did not respond, and unlike the 2022 edition it counts games and services made for third parties, educational games and advergames. Its own chart sets 251.6 million dollars for 2022 beside 143.3 million for 2021 and 149.9 million for 2018 on the earlier basis, a change the survey says it made at the risk of losing direct comparison.
Market size.source: Abragames and ApexBrasil, 2023 Brazilian Gaming Industry Survey by GA Consulting, trade body survey

Shape.claim: 75.3 percent of the Brazilians aged 16 to 55 that Pesquisa Game Brasil surveyed in March 2026 play digital games, down from 82.8 percent in the 2025 edition. Women are 52.8 percent of players, and 44.1 percent prefer the phone, against 24 percent the console and 21.1 percent the PC.
Shape.source: Pesquisa Game Brasil 2026, by SX Group and Go Gamers with Blend New Research and ESPM, reported by Meio & Mensagem, 9 April 2026, marketing trade press

Shape.claim: Quote Pesquisa Game Brasil with its edition and sample, because it publishes no headcount and its sample and findings swing between editions. It heard 14,825 people in January 2023, about 6,282 in 2025 and 7,115 aged 16 to 55 in March 2026, and found men a majority of players in 2023 and women in 2022 and 2026.
Shape.source: Go Gamers, Pesquisa Game Brasil 2023 release, survey publisher, with its 2022 release and press reports of the 2025 and 2026 editions

Shape.claim: 38 percent of internet users aged 10 and over played online in the previous three months in TIC Domicílios 2025, as in 2023 and 2024, 45 percent of men and 31 percent of women. Among those aged 10 to 15 the share fell from 89 to 80 percent, and among those 60 and over it rose from 9 to 15.
Shape.source: Cetic.br (NIC.br), TIC Domicílios 2025, table C7, national household survey, with the 2023 and 2024 editions' tables

Shape.claim: Abragames' 2023 survey estimates 1,042 studios and 13,225 people working at them in 2022, 58 percent of the studios in the Southeast. 58 percent of developers sold abroad, mainly to the United States and Latin America, and 44 percent of studios name computers as the platform that earns them most.
Shape.source: Abragames and ApexBrasil, Brazil Games Industry Fact Sheet 2023, trade body survey

Shape.claim: Do not read Abragames' studio chart as a growth series. Its 133, 375, 1,009 and 1,042 developers set the respondents of the 2014 and 2018 censuses beside the estimated totals of the 2022 and 2023 surveys, so the 177 percent growth since 2018 the 2023 report quotes compares one kind of count with the other.
Shape.source: Abragames and ApexBrasil, 2023 Brazilian Gaming Industry Survey by GA Consulting, trade body survey

Shape.claim: Wildlife Studios led Brazil's developers on both of the trade body's measures. Abragames' 2022 survey found it the revenue leader in 2015, 2018 and 2021 among Brazilian developers with games in AppMagic's 500 top-grossing apps, and names the ten largest by LinkedIn headcount as Wildlife, Afterverse, Aquiris, Fanatee, Puga, Sioux, Kokku, Gazeus, Pipa and Tapps.
Shape.source: Abragames and ApexBrasil, Pesquisa da Indústria Brasileira de Games 2022, by Homo Ludens, trade body survey

Shape.claim: Epic Games has owned a Brazilian studio since 2023. AQUIRIS, the Porto Alegre developer of Horizon Chase and Wonderbox, announced on 19 April 2023 that it was joining Epic Games as Epic Games Brasil, Epic's first studio in Latin America, to make content within Fortnite.
Shape.source: AQUIRIS news, 19 April 2023, company announcement

Shape.claim: Riot Games runs Brazil's League of Legends league itself, and restores it as an independent league in 2026: after a year inside the League of the Americas, the CBLOL (Campeonato Brasileiro de League of Legends) returns under its own name, with one place each at First Stand, the Mid-Season Invitational and the World Championship.
Shape.source: LoL Esports (Riot Games), 'O CBLOL está de volta!', 29 September 2025, league organiser announcement

Press structure.claim: TecMundo and its games desk, Voxel, belong to a national newspaper group. Estadão announced on 1 October 2025 that it had bought No Zebra Network (NZN), which controls TecMundo, Voxel, Minha Série, Mega Curioso and The Brief, and now holds 100 percent of it. H.I.G. Capital had controlled NZN until then, and the price was not disclosed.
Press structure.source: TecMundo, 1 October 2025, the acquired company's own outlet

Press structure.claim: A retailer owns Jovem Nerd, a geek-culture media brand whose programmes cover games among other subjects. Magazine Luiza (Magalu) announced on 14 April 2021 that it was buying Jovem Nerd, which it called the country's largest and most iconic multimedia platform for the nerd and geek audience, adding it to the technology site Canaltech, bought about six months earlier, to build audience for its advertising business, MagaluAds.
Press structure.source: Magazine Luiza press release, 14 April 2021, primary corporate disclosure

Press structure.claim: IGN Brasil, the Brazilian edition of IGN, is a Webedia site, as its own footer states.
Press structure.source: IGN Brasil site footer, September 2026, publisher self-disclosure

Press structure.claim: The group that publishes Omelete runs games events as well as media. Omelete&CO describes itself as the largest independent entertainment company in Latin America, lists CCXP and gamescom latam, the Latin American edition of gamescom, among its brands beside the Omelete portal, and says its partnership with Gaules and Baiano gives it access to Brazil's Counter-Strike and League of Legends player communities.
Press structure.source: Omelete&CO company site, company self-description

Press structure.claim: The Counter-Strike news site DRAFT5 is owned by the platform whose competitive scene it covers. DRAFT5, founded in February 2017, was bought in June 2019 by Gamers Club, which it calls the main Counter-Strike platform in Latin America, and since 2020 has been part of Gamers Club Media, a network of single-game sites such as VZone (VALORANT) and Tropa FF (Free Fire).
Press structure.source: DRAFT5 Sobre nós (about) page, publisher self-description

Press structure.claim: Drops de Jogos sits inside a newspaper portal as a partner, not a property. Created by Pedro Zambarda in 2015 and served from the UAI portal's domain, it describes itself as a partner of Portal Uai, the newspaper O Estado de Minas and Diários Associados, and as part of the Rede Progressista de Games (Progressive Games Network), which it says took part, covering and contributing, in the passage of Lei 14.852, the Marco Legal dos Games, in 2024.
Press structure.source: Drops de Jogos Sobre e Expediente (about and masthead) page, publisher self-description

Press structure.claim: The defining pattern of the Brazilian games press is that the titles whose owners could be verified are one line of business inside groups whose main trade is something other than games journalism: a newspaper (Estadão, TecMundo and Voxel), a retailer (Magalu, Jovem Nerd and Canaltech), an international digital publisher (Webedia, IGN Brasil), an entertainment and events group (Omelete&CO) and an esports platform (Gamers Club, DRAFT5). Founder-led sites sit beside them, some as partners of newspaper portals, as Drops de Jogos is of UAI. This is an interpretation resting on the ownership claims above.
Press structure.source: TecMundo, 1 October 2025, plus the ownership rows above

Press structure.claim: Do not state who owns Adrenaline or Outer Space. Outer Space's footer names only its operating company, Outer Space Media Ltda., with no parent or shareholders, and Adrenaline's own pages, including the Quem somos (about) page that search results summarise as naming its two founders, answered scripted requests with a Cloudflare browser check on 28 September 2026, so neither ownership could be verified to standard. Open Adrenaline's Quem somos page in a browser to confirm its founders.
Press structure.source: No source meeting this directory's standard

Press structure.claim: Do not cite The Enemy as a live games outlet without checking. Omelete billed its gamescom latam 2025 games showcase as the successor to The Enemy Direct, and on 28 September 2026 theenemy.com.br answered with a permanent redirect to omelete.com.br, but no statement from Omelete&CO on whether or when The Enemy closed was found.
Press structure.source: Omelete, 29 April 2025, the owner's own outlet

Venues.claim: WhatsApp chats are private. 66 percent of Brazilian internet users aged 9 to 17 use their own WhatsApp profile at least weekly, level with Instagram and ahead of TikTok at 57 percent, and none of WhatsApp's conversation is publicly searchable. That its chats are private is a reading of the product type, not a survey finding.
Venues.source: Cetic.br (NIC.br), TIC Kids Online Brasil 2025, table C8, national survey of children and adolescents

Venues.claim: Discord servers are private, and Discord's live video is suspended in Brazil. The data protection authority, ANPD, ordered Discord on 12 August 2026 to suspend Go Live, used for live streams in private servers, until it proves it protects children and adolescents. The platform itself is not blocked. That its servers are private reads the product type, not the order.
Venues.card_text: Discord servers are private, and Go Live suspended
Venues.source: ANPD news release, 12 August 2026, data protection authority

Venues.claim: Do not read one streaming platform's data as Brazil's. Streams Charts calls multistreaming a core competitive advantage in Brazil: Gaules and Baiano, second and fourth among Brazilian streamers by hours watched in 2025, each broadcast on Twitch, YouTube and Kick at once, and its ranking is not games-only either.
Venues.card_text: Streamers use three platforms at once
Venues.source: Streams Charts, Top Brazilian streamers of 2025, 18 December 2025, analytics platform

Venues.claim: X was off in Brazil for five and a half weeks in 2024, so Brazilian X data has a gap from 30 August to 8 October 2024. The Supreme Court suspended X nationwide for repeated non-compliance with its decisions, and authorised its return once the company complied and paid its fines.
Venues.card_text: X suspended nationwide, 30 Aug to 8 Oct 2024
Venues.source: Supremo Tribunal Federal news release, 8 October 2024, supreme court

Venues.claim: Do not assert a Brazilian games venue hierarchy, or repeat a board's claim to be the largest. The national surveys count activities and profiles, not what is discussed, Pesquisa Game Brasil's free report sits behind a lead form, and no independent measure of any Brazilian board's scale was found.
Venues.source: Sources checked and found not to contain the needed data, documented gap

Unique to this market.claim: A ClassInd rating is required before sale, and it informs rather than bans. Under Portaria MJSP nº 1.048 of 15 October 2025, which replaced Portaria 502/2021 and has been in force since 17 November 2025, no game may be sold without a Classificação Indicativa (ClassInd) rating: games on physical media go through the Justice Ministry's prior analysis, and digital-only games rate themselves through the International Age Rating Coalition (IARC) questionnaire, which the ministry checks by sampling. The portaria defines the rating as pedagogical and informative and forbids it from prohibiting the showing of a work, cutting scenes or asking for content to be removed. It added a 6 band, so the scale runs L, 6, 10, 12, 14, 16 and 18, and made interactivity a rating axis.
Unique to this market.card_text: Ratings are required, and they inform rather than ban
Unique to this market.source: Portaria MJSP nº 1.048/2025, Ministério da Justiça e Segurança Pública, primary legal text

Unique to this market.claim: Paid loot boxes are barred to under-18s, but the game itself is not. The only express prohibition on games in the ECA Digital (Estatuto Digital da Criança e do Adolescente, Lei 15.211/2025), in force since 17 March 2026, is on loot boxes for children and adolescents, and a game complies by offering a version without them or by switching them off until the player proves they are an adult, according to the government's question-and-answer guide to the law.
Unique to this market.card_text: Loot boxes are banned for under-18s
Unique to this market.source: Perguntas e respostas sobre o ECA Digital, ANPD, Ministério da Justiça e Segurança Pública and Secom, updated 30 July 2026, government guidance

Unique to this market.claim: Games that children are likely to use must ship parental controls switched on. Since 17 March 2026 the ECA Digital requires any service aimed at or likely to be used by minors, online games included, to offer tools to limit and monitor time of use, with default settings at the highest level of protection, and requires games with text, voice or video contact between users to limit those features by default so that a parent consents. It sets no cap on play.
Unique to this market.card_text: Parental controls on by default, time limits included
Unique to this market.source: Lei 15.211/2025 (ECA Digital), articles 17 and 21, Planalto, primary legal text

Unique to this market.claim: Games have their own law, and betting is written out of it. The Marco Legal dos Games (the games legal framework, Lei 14.852 of 3 May 2024) frees the making, import and sale of games from prior state authorisation, and says lotteries, bets and any game offering a bet with prizes in real or virtual assets, or with a random or predicted result, are not jogos eletrônicos and get none of its benefits. It opens the culture incentive laws, the Lei Rouanet and the Lei do Audiovisual, to game development, and requires in-game purchase tools to restrict purchases by children by default.
Unique to this market.card_text: Games have their own law, and bets are not games
Unique to this market.source: Lei 14.852/2024 (Marco Legal dos Games), Planalto, primary legal text

Unique to this market.claim: Foreign providers need a legal representative in Brazil. Article 40 of the ECA Digital requires every provider it covers, online games and app stores included, to keep a legal representative in the country able to receive summonses and answer to the authorities, and a foreign company's Brazilian branch or office is jointly liable for its fines, which reach 10 percent of the group's revenue in Brazil.
Unique to this market.card_text: Foreign providers need a legal representative
Unique to this market.source: Lei 15.211/2025 (ECA Digital), articles 35 and 40, Planalto, primary legal text

Unique to this market.claim: Betting is banned, by a provisional measure. Medida Provisória nº 1.394 of 25 September 2026, which has the force of law from publication, prohibits fixed-odds betting in Brazil, on sports and on online games decided by a random number generator alike, including by operators abroad serving people in Brazil. Licensed operators must take their sites and apps offline within ten days, every licence ends thirty days after publication, and all betting advertising and sponsorship is banned.
Unique to this market.card_text: Betting and its sponsorship are banned
Unique to this market.source: Medida Provisória nº 1.394/2026, Planalto, primary legal text

Unique to this market.claim: HOLD: do not report the betting ban as settled law. Medida Provisória 1.394 took effect on publication on 25 September 2026, and the Congress record sets its deliberation period at 25 September to 23 November 2026, with an urgency regime from 9 November. Report it as in force and provisional, and check the record before quoting it.
Unique to this market.source: Congresso Nacional, MPV 1394/2026 record, legislature

Unique to this market.claim: Consoles pay a 20 percent federal tax on industrialised products (Imposto sobre Produtos Industrializados, IPI). The Receita Federal's IPI table (TIPI), updated to 30 January 2026, sets 20 percent for video game consoles, 9 percent for their parts and accessories and 0 percent for video game machines with a built-in screen, portable or not.
Unique to this market.card_text: Consoles pay 20 percent IPI
Unique to this market.source: Receita Federal, Tabela de Incidência do IPI (TIPI), updated to 30 January 2026, tax authority

Unique to this market.claim: The IPI on consoles may end in 2027. Constitutional Amendment 132 of 20 December 2023 reduces IPI rates to zero from 2027 except on products with incentivised industrialisation in the Manaus Free Trade Zone, and whether consoles are among them could not be verified, so check before quoting the 20 percent for 2027 or later. The same reform's Lei Complementar 214 of 16 January 2025 creates three new taxes, IBS, CBS and the Imposto Seletivo.
Unique to this market.card_text: Console IPI may end in 2027
Unique to this market.source: Emenda Constitucional nº 132/2023, Planalto, primary legal text

Unique to this market.claim: Games can raise money through the Lei Rouanet. Instrução Normativa MinC nº 29 of 29 January 2026, which sets the procedures of the Lei Rouanet's incentive mechanism for cultural projects (Lei 8.313/1991) and revoked Instrução Normativa nº 23 of 5 February 2025, lets a game project seek up to 1.5 million reais and the development of a game, a production phase ending in a playable simulation or demonstration that shows its potential, up to 400,000 reais, the same limits the 2025 instruction set. Higher sums are allowed for audiovisual projects chosen in a public call or holding a contract that secures at least half the amount sought, at market prices.
Unique to this market.card_text: Lei Rouanet: up to 1.5 million reais a game
Unique to this market.source: Instrução Normativa MinC nº 29, de 29 de janeiro de 2026, Ministério da Cultura, published in the Diário Oficial da União on 30 January 2026, primary legal text

Unique to this market.claim: São Paulo state funds games through its cultural programme, ProAC. Its 2026 games call, Edital Fomento CultSP – ProAC nº 05/2026, offers 6 million reais, 300,000 reais each for ten projects developing a game up to a functional prototype (vertical slice) or a playable demo and ten finishing and publishing one. It is open to proponents based in the state with at least two years of activity, and the list of applications published after registration closed counts 217, 174 for development and 43 for finishing and publishing.
Unique to this market.card_text: São Paulo state: 6 million reais for games in 2026
Unique to this market.source: Edital Fomento CultSP – ProAC nº 05/2026 and its list of applications, Secretaria da Cultura, Economia e Indústria Criativas do Estado de São Paulo, state funding call

Unique to this market.claim: HOLD: do not describe ANCINE's rules for publicly financing games as written. The film agency's Agenda Regulatória 2026/2027, approved by its board and announced on 30 March 2026, lists as Action 18 the regulation of how publicly financed games projects are approved, executed, monitored and accounted for under the Marco Legal dos Games, because the absence of specific rules limits the segment's access to the existing support mechanisms, and expects to finish it in the first half of 2027; Action 6, on the same timetable, would set the registration and reporting duties of companies in the games chain. The same agenda plans a general regulation of the Fundo Setorial do Audiovisual (Action 11), so check with ANCINE before citing a line of the fund for games.
Unique to this market.source: ANCINE, Agenda Regulatória 2026/2027, approved by Deliberação de Diretoria Colegiada nº 276-E/2026, regulator's own agenda

Unique to this market.claim: Android accounted for 75.45 percent of mobile page views in Brazil in August 2026 and iOS for 24.54 percent, per StatCounter, which bases its shares on page views, over 3 billion a month by its own account, so the split measures web traffic, not devices, players or spending.
Unique to this market.card_text: Android ~75 percent of mobile web traffic
Unique to this market.source: StatCounter Global Stats, mobile operating system market share in Brazil, August 2026, web analytics

Unique to this market.claim: Do not say which store Brazilians spend most through on mobile, because no free source read splits Brazilian mobile games spending between Google Play and the App Store. Sensor Tower's Brazilian figures, as the trade press relays them, combine the two stores; StatCounter's Android and iOS shares count web traffic, not spending; and the App Store's top-grossing feed ranks games without revenue, while Google Play shows no chart for Brazil. Read a vendor's per-store figure, where one is published, as that vendor's estimate.
Unique to this market.source: Sources checked and found not to contain the needed data, documented gap

Unique to this market.claim: Nintendo's eShop sells in Brazil in reais and takes Visa and Mastercard credit cards, not PayPal. Players without a card can buy its gift cards on Nintendo's own store with Pix or boleto, and Nintendo content cards are sold at retailers such as Lojas Americanas and Magazine Luiza, and its digital games at americanas.com, submarino.com and Nuuvem, per Nintendo's support pages.
Unique to this market.card_text: Pix and boleto buy Nintendo gift cards
Unique to this market.source: Nintendo support, Perguntas frequentes sobre o Nintendo Switch eShop do Brasil, undated, platform owner's support page

Unique to this market.claim: Nintendo's consoles had no official distribution in Brazil from January 2015 to September 2020. Nintendo stopped distributing its consoles and games in Brazil in January 2015, saying challenges in the local business environment had made its distribution model unsustainable, returned officially with the Switch on 18 September 2020 at a suggested 2,999 reais, distributed by Ingram Micro rather than made in the country, and launched the Switch 2 in Brazil on 5 June 2025, the worldwide date, at 4,499.90 reais.
Unique to this market.card_text: Nintendo official again since 2020
Unique to this market.source: TechTudo, 4 September 2020, technology news site, with Exame, 9 January 2015, and CNN Brasil, 23 April 2025

Unique to this market.claim: Sony and Microsoft launched their current consoles officially in Brazil in November 2020 and cut the announced prices before launch after an IPI reduction. Sony set 19 November 2020 for the PlayStation 5 and on 3 November 2020 cut its suggested prices, which it said was a result of the new IPI reduction for games, from 4,499 to 4,199 reais for the Digital Edition and from 4,999 to 4,699 reais for the model with an Ultra HD Blu-ray drive; Microsoft set 10 November 2020 for the Xbox Series X and Series S and on 29 October 2020 cut them from 4,999 and 2,999 reais to 4,599 and 2,799 reais.
Unique to this market.card_text: PS5 and Xbox Series official since November 2020
Unique to this market.source: PlayStation.Blog BR, 3 November 2020, company announcement, with Xbox Wire em Português, 23 October 2020, and TechTudo, 29 October 2020

Where the data lives.claim: Pesquisa Game Brasil (PGB). The annual consumer survey Go Gamers publishes, in its 13th edition in 2026, gives the share of Brazilians aged 16 to 55 who say they play, with their gender, age, class and preferred device. A free Trend Report sits behind a registration form, and the full data is sold by subscription from 2,290 reais a month.
Where the data lives.source: Pesquisa Game Brasil, Go Gamers, commercial annual survey

Where the data lives.claim: Pesquisa da Indústria Brasileira de Games (Brazilian Games Industry Survey), Abragames. The developers' association's survey with ApexBrasil counts studios and the people at them, where they are and how many sell abroad, free as reports and fact sheets. The 2023 survey, which portrays 2022, is the latest published.
Where the data lives.card_text: Pesquisa da Indústria Brasileira de Games (Abragames)
Where the data lives.source: Abragames with ApexBrasil, industry association survey

Where the data lives.claim: TIC Domicílios and TIC Kids Online Brasil, Cetic.br. The annual surveys of internet use run at NIC.br ask whether internet users aged 10 and over played online, and whether children and adolescents bought anything in online games, with free tables in Portuguese, English and Spanish. TIC Domicílios 2025 was presented on 9 December 2025.
Where the data lives.card_text: TIC Domicílios and TIC Kids Online Brasil (Cetic.br)
Where the data lives.source: Cetic.br, NIC.br, annual household surveys

Where the data lives.claim: IBGE PNAD Contínua, in the Sistema de Informações e Indicadores Culturais (SIIC). The national statistics office's household survey asks internet users aged 10 and over what they went online for: 30.3 percent went online to play in 2024. The SIIC is free and published every two years; the latest came out on 12 December 2025.
Where the data lives.source: IBGE Sistema de Informações e Indicadores Culturais 2013-2024, 12 December 2025, national statistics office

Where the data lives.claim: ClassInd (Classificação Indicativa) games consultation, Ministério da Justiça e Segurança Pública. The ministry's portal lists the rating it gave each game, free, on the scale L, 6, 10, 12, 14, 16 and 18, and its rating decisions are published as portarias; the rating informs rather than restricts, and complaints that a rating does not match a game go to the ministry's ombudsman.
Where the data lives.source: ClassInd portal, Ministério da Justiça e Segurança Pública, rating body

Where the data lives.claim: The State of Video Gaming, Matthew Ball and Epyllion. A free annual analyst presentation with market sizing, participation and platform charts for most major markets, useful for cross market comparison that no single free source provides. It aggregates many vendors rather than applying one methodology, so treat figures as the analyst assembly they are and cite the underlying source where the deck names one.
Where the data lives.card_text: The State of Video Gaming (Ball, Epyllion)
Where the data lives.source: Matthew Ball, Epyllion, independent analyst, annual presentation

Where the data lives.claim: Abragames' industry survey has no fixed calendar, so quote the edition with the figure. The 2022 edition covers 2020 and 2021, the 2023 edition measures 2022 and was published on 28 February 2024, and a third edition, run with Go Gamers, began sending questionnaires in September 2026 with no publication date.
Where the data lives.source: The Gaming Era, 17 September 2026, games business news site

Where the data lives.claim: Steam weekly top sellers for Brazil, Valve. Valve's own ranking of the top 100 products on Steam in Brazil by revenue, free, published every Tuesday for the week before, with each title's rank the week before. It gives ranks, not units or revenue, covers Steam alone, and a script can read it through the store's web API without a key.
Where the data lives.source: Valve, Steam Charts weekly top sellers for Brazil, platform chart

Where the data lives.claim: App Store top-grossing games feed for Brazil, Apple. Apple's public RSS feed ranks the top-grossing games in the Brazilian App Store, free, with prices in reais and the time of its last update, and a script can read it as JSON. It gives ranks, not revenue, states neither its method nor its period, and covers Apple's store alone.
Where the data lives.card_text: App Store top-grossing games feed, Brazil (Apple)
Where the data lives.source: Apple, iTunes Store RSS feed Top rentáveis, Jogos, Brazil, platform chart

known_gaps.gap: Consumer spending. No free figure for what Brazilian players spend is held: the size card sizes studios' revenue, and the consumer figures in circulation are unsourced or relay a paid vendor.
known_gaps.instead: Take a consumer figure from Newzoo's own release, with its basis and year, as the Standing notes say, and read a figure in reais with no named publisher as untraceable.

known_gaps.gap: Who spends, and on what. Spending by platform and by payer, and in-game purchases beyond whether children made any, are not held: Pesquisa Game Brasil sells its cross-tabs by subscription.
known_gaps.instead: Read the free PGB Trend Report behind its registration form for the headlines and the Cetic.br tables for children's purchases in games, and say which sample a share is of.

known_gaps.gap: Mobile and streaming data are not tagged to Brazil. Sensor Tower, AppMagic, Streams Charts and Esports Charts are Global rows, so a BR-filtered search returns none of them, though Abragames models studio revenue partly from AppMagic.
known_gaps.instead: Search the Data group without a market filter, and read a vendor's Brazil figure as that house's estimate.

known_gaps.gap: Company filings. No Brazilian games company files where a reader can use it, and Sea, which owns Free Fire's publisher Garena, reports it with no country split.
known_gaps.instead: Read the global publishers' IR rows the directory holds, and only where they name Brazil; treat a studio's Brazilian address as a location until its owner is checked.

known_gaps.gap: Communities, and what players think. No Brazilian review venue is held, and the activity of the forums and subreddits held could not be checked: Fórum Adrenaline answered with a bot check and Reddit refused scripted reads.
known_gaps.instead: Read the held forums and subreddits, and the Steam reviews and forums row filtered to Brazilian Portuguese, as temperature, never as size, and check a thread's recent post dates before naming it as a venue.

known_gaps.gap: Video channels. They carry no market tag by design, so a BR-filtered search returns none.
known_gaps.instead: Search channels by language Portuguese instead.

player_population.source: Núcleo de Informação e Coordenação do Ponto BR (NIC.br) and Comitê Gestor da Internet no Brasil (CGI.br), TIC Domicílios 2025
player_population.definition: Internet users aged 10 and over in Brazil who played online in the three months before the interview. They were 38 percent of internet users, as the survey's table of totals states (sheet C7). The question asks only about playing online, so play without a connection is not in it. The data comes from TIC Domicílios 2025, the household survey NIC.br runs for CGI.br, with face-to-face interviews of 24,535 individuals in 27,177 households from March to August 2025.

Standing.claim: Do not quote a revenue rank for India from its annuals, because neither FICCI-EY nor Lumikai states one, and do not call India the largest market by downloads without the basis. Sensor Tower calls India the world's largest mobile gaming market by downloads, 8.45 billion installs in FY 2024-25, counting the App Store and Google Play only, which leaves China's Android stores out, while Lumikai's FY24 report calls India the second largest by mobile gaming downloads. Quote a rank with its ranker, its basis and its year.
Standing.source: Sensor Tower, India Mobile Game Insights 2025, June 2025, analytics vendor blog, with Lumikai FY24 executive summary

Standing.claim: India ranks sixth in Asia-Pacific by mobile in-app purchase revenue in 2025, at 800 million dollars, and first in Asia by game downloads, at 7.95 billion, per India's State of Play, written by Naavik for MIXI Global Investments in July 2026 from Sensor Tower data and combined industry estimates. Its revenue table counts China through iOS alone.
Standing.source: Naavik for MIXI Global Investments, India's State of Play, July 2026, investor report

Market size.claim: Video games and esports in India earn 63 billion rupees in 2025, up from 57 billion in 2024, per the FICCI-EY media and entertainment report Stories, scale and impact, released 24 March 2026. The EY estimate is domestic revenue gross of taxes: in-app purchases 36 billion rupees, advertising 15 billion and esports 12 billion.
Market size.card_text: 63 billion rupees video games and esports revenue
Market size.source: FICCI-EY, Stories, scale and impact: Unlocking India's media and entertainment economy, 24 March 2026, trade body and consultancy annual

Market size.claim: The FICCI-EY games figure is revenue, not consumer spend, and each edition redraws and restates the segment. The 2026 edition splits Online and video games into Money gaming, 133 billion rupees for 2025 counted only up to the ban, and Esports and video games, 63 billion. The 2025 edition called them transaction-based games and esports and casual, and put the second at 53 billion for 2024, which the 2026 edition restates as 57 billion. Quote the edition with the figure.
Market size.source: FICCI-EY, Stories, scale and impact: Unlocking India's media and entertainment economy, 24 March 2026, trade body and consultancy annual

Market size.claim: The two annuals size the same 2025 market on different bases, and FICCI-EY says they do not reconcile. FICCI-EY prints Lumikai's own figures on a page Lumikai supplied, 1,534 million dollars for 2025, and notes that this revenue data does not tie in to EY estimates and has to be seen directionally. Name the publisher and the basis with every Indian games figure.
Market size.source: FICCI-EY, Stories, scale and impact: Unlocking India's media and entertainment economy, 24 March 2026, trade body and consultancy annual, page powered by Lumikai

Market size.claim: Do not read Lumikai's report as a fiscal-year series released each autumn, or compare its 2025 games figure with earlier headlines. The FY24 edition, posted in November 2024, covered April 2023 to March 2024 and put the market at 3.8 billion dollars, 2.4 billion of it real-money gaming. The 2025 edition, released on 23 March 2026, covers calendar 2025 and leaves real-money gaming out of its 1.5 billion dollars.
Market size.source: Lumikai, State of India Interactive Media & Gaming FY'24 executive summary, as hosted by InvestGame, venture fund annual

Market size.claim: Take FICCI-EY's online gaming series from one edition, because each edition restates past years. The March 2025 edition, Shape the future, which is not the separate EY report A studio called India made for the WAVES summit, gave 236 billion rupees for 2023 and 232 billion for 2024, a 2 percent fall, and within it 2022 reads 222 billion in the overview and 196 billion in the gaming chapter. Transaction-based games were 179 billion of the 2024 figure.
Market size.source: FICCI-EY, Shape the future, March 2025, trade body and consultancy annual

Shape.claim: Lumikai counts 555 million gamers in India in 2025, 9 percent fewer than in 2024, and puts the fall down to the ban on money games.
Shape.source: Lumikai, State of Interactive Media Report 2025, fifth edition, 23 March 2026, venture fund annual

Shape.claim: In Lumikai's survey of smartphone users, 45 percent of players are women, 44 percent are aged 18 to 30, and 97 percent play on a phone.
Shape.source: FICCI-EY, Stories, scale and impact: Unlocking India's media and entertainment economy, 24 March 2026, trade body and consultancy annual, page powered by Lumikai, survey of 3,000+ smartphone users

Shape.claim: Free Fire and Battlegrounds Mobile India earned the most of any games in India in 2025, ahead of Coin Master, Candy Crush Saga and eFootball.
Shape.source: Lumikai, State of Interactive Media Report 2025, fifth edition, 23 March 2026, venture fund annual

Shape.claim: India had over 1,900 game development companies in 2024, employing around 66,000 people by one count and over 130,000 by another.
Shape.source: EY, A studio called India, May 2025, consultancy report for the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting's WAVES 2025

Shape.claim: Games made in India earned over 1.5 billion dollars abroad in 2025-26, by the developers' association's own count, which EY did not verify.
Shape.source: FICCI-EY, Stories, scale and impact: Unlocking India's media and entertainment economy, 24 March 2026, trade body and consultancy annual, data compiled by the Game Developer Association of India
