Shape.claim: Nazara, JetSynthesys and nCore publish games in India, Gametion, SuperGaming and Gameberry Labs make their own, and Electronic Arts, Krafton, Rockstar, Ubisoft and Riot Games all work there.
Shape.source: EY, A studio called India, May 2025, consultancy report for the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting's WAVES 2025

Shape.claim: The two annuals count players in opposite directions, FICCI-EY at 515 to 525 million and rising, Lumikai at 555 million and falling, and neither says who it counted.
Shape.source: FICCI-EY, Stories, scale and impact: Unlocking India's media and entertainment economy, 24 March 2026, trade body and consultancy annual

Shape.claim: Device shares overlap and do not sum, and Lumikai's 97 percent on a phone comes from a panel of smartphone users, not all players.
Shape.source: FICCI-EY, Stories, scale and impact: Unlocking India's media and entertainment economy, 24 March 2026, trade body and consultancy annual

Press structure.claim: IGN India is a licensed edition, not an IGN-owned site. Its footer says it is operated by Fork Media Group Pvt. Ltd. under license from IGN Entertainment and its affiliates.
Press structure.source: IGN India site footer, September 2026, publisher self-disclosure

Press structure.claim: Outlook Respawn is the gaming, esports and pop culture vertical of Outlook India. Outlook Publishing (India) Pvt. Ltd. says it is part of the Rajan Raheja group, whose interests run from real estate, cement and automotive batteries to hospitality and media.
Press structure.source: Outlook About Us page, company self-description

Press structure.claim: Moneycontrol belongs to Reliance Industries' media arm. Network18 runs moneycontrol.com, and Independent Media Trust, whose sole beneficiary is Reliance Industries, and other promoter group entities hold 56.89 percent of Network18, per CARE Ratings on 16 December 2024.
Press structure.source: CARE Ratings press release on Network 18 Media and Investments Limited, 16 December 2024, credit rating agency

Press structure.claim: Storyboard18, whose gaming desk covers policy and the real-money gaming industry, is Network18's advertising and marketing trade title. Its own site describes it as Network18 Group's flagship platform focussed on the advertising and marketing community.
Press structure.source: Storyboard18 gaming news page, site metadata, publisher self-description

Press structure.claim: AFK Gaming, the esports and games outlet, is being bought outright by NODWIN Gaming. Nazara Technologies' annual report for 2024-25 says NODWIN agreed on 18 December 2024 to buy the remaining 92.30 percent of AFK Gaming for 7.58 crore rupees, in cash and a swap of shares, with completion expected in 2025-26, after which AFK would be a wholly owned subsidiary. Completion was not verified.
Press structure.source: Nazara Technologies annual report 2024-25, directors' report, listed company filing

Press structure.claim: NODWIN Gaming, AFK Gaming's owner, is no longer a Nazara subsidiary. Nazara ceased to hold a controlling stake in the July to September 2025 quarter, after it stayed out of a NODWIN fundraise, and NODWIN became an associate, with Nazara still its largest shareholder.
Press structure.source: Indian Startup News, 14 November 2025, reporting Nazara's Q2 FY26 results, startup news site

Press structure.claim: AFK Gaming sells services to brands in the field it covers. Its site says it also operates a full-stack services agency, Max Level by AFK Gaming, to help brands grow in the gaming and esports space.
Press structure.source: AFK Gaming site, publisher self-description

Press structure.claim: Do not cite India Today Gaming as a live outlet without checking. The site, copyright Living Media India Limited, still answered on 30 September 2026, but the newest items on its homepage were dated 30 July 2025, and no statement on whether it closed was found.
Press structure.source: India Today Gaming homepage, read 30 September 2026, publisher's own site

Press structure.claim: Sportskeeda belongs to Nazara Technologies, the listed games company. Nazara bought the last 8.97 percent of Absolute Sports, Sportskeeda's parent, in March 2025, taking its stake to 100 percent.
Press structure.source: Inc42, 19 March 2025, startup trade press

Press structure.claim: The defining pattern of the Indian games press is that most outlets whose owners could be verified are verticals or trade titles of national media groups whose main business is general or business news: Outlook (the Rajan Raheja group), Network18 (Reliance Industries), Bennett, Coleman (The Economic Times) and Living Media (India Today Gaming). The other pattern is the games industry owning its press: Sportskeeda belongs to Nazara, and AFK Gaming is being bought outright by NODWIN Gaming, whose largest shareholder is Nazara. IGN India is a licensed edition run by an advertising company. This is an interpretation resting on the ownership claims above.
Press structure.source: Outlook About Us page, company self-description, plus the ownership rows above

Venues.claim: YouTube is where Indian live streams are watched. Streams Charts says India's livestreaming remains dominated by YouTube Live, and all ten of the country's most-watched streamers in April 2026 streamed there, but only one, LoLzZz Gaming, streams games; the rest are devotional, cooking and cricket channels.
Venues.source: Streams Charts, Top Indian streamers April 2026, 6 May 2026, analytics platform

Venues.claim: The most-watched Indian games streamer on YouTube in 2025 was LoLzZz Gaming, Yash Thakker, who streams Battlegrounds Mobile India. He was tenth worldwide among YouTube gaming streamers with 29,884,524 hours watched, the only Indian in Streams Charts' top ten.
Venues.card_text: LoLzZz Gaming, India's most-watched games streamer
Venues.source: Streams Charts, Top YouTube gaming streamers of 2025, 19 December 2025, analytics platform

Venues.claim: WhatsApp chats are private, so they cannot be read from outside. The government put India's WhatsApp users at 53 crore in February 2021, ahead of YouTube at 44.8 crore, Facebook at 41 crore and Instagram at 21 crore, figures it took from outside portals. That its chats are private is a reading of the product, not the release.
Venues.source: Press Information Bureau release on the IT Rules 2021, 25 February 2021, government release

Venues.claim: Only members can read a Discord server, but anyone can see how many it has. Discord's invite page showed about 495,484 members, 5,356 of them online, for the official BATTLEGROUNDS MOBILE INDIA server on 30 September 2026.
Venues.source: Discord invite page for the official BATTLEGROUNDS MOBILE INDIA server, read 30 September 2026, platform's own count

Venues.claim: Do not assert an Indian games venue hierarchy beyond Streams Charts' YouTube datum. The government's 2021 platform figures count all use, not games, and Niko Partners' India Gamer Behavior and Market Insights Report of October 2025 ranks kinds of channel, social media 58.7 percent, short video apps 46.6 percent, influencers and streamers 45.3 percent, not named venues.
Venues.source: Niko Partners, What you need to know about India's video game market, 5 November 2025, market research firm

Unique to this market.claim: There is no Indian games rating board, and no Indian law requires a game to carry an age rating. The Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act, 2025 and its 2026 Rules set no rating scale, and the Act lists, among steps the government may take, "supporting initiatives aimed at increasing public access to safe and age-appropriate social gaming content". India has no rating authority in the International Age Rating Coalition (IARC), whose questionnaire gives a generic rating for the rest of the world, so storefronts that use IARC show that generic rating in India.
Unique to this market.source: Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act, 2025 (Act No. 32 of 2025), section 4, MeitY, primary legal text, with IARC, About, read 30 September 2026

Unique to this market.claim: Online games played for money are banned, whether they turn on skill or chance. The Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act, 2025 defines an online money game as one played by paying fees or depositing money or other stakes in expectation of winning, and bans offering one, advertising one and any bank or payment transfer for one. Other stakes include coins, tokens or credits bought with money, real or virtual.
Unique to this market.card_text: Money games are banned, skill or chance
Unique to this market.source: Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act, 2025 (Act No. 32 of 2025), sections 2, 5, 6 and 7, MeitY, primary legal text

Unique to this market.claim: Most games need no licence or registration. Under the Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Rules, 2026, in force since 1 May 2026, a game must be registered with the Online Gaming Authority of India only if it is to be offered as an e-sport or if the central government notifies it, or its category, for registration, having regard to risk to children, scale, money flows and the provider's country of origin. The Authority may also examine any game of its own motion to decide whether it is a money game.
Unique to this market.card_text: Only esports must register
Unique to this market.source: Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Rules, 2026, G.S.R. 303(E), 22 April 2026, rules 8 and 12, MeitY, primary legal text

Unique to this market.claim: An e-sport is a legal category in India, and it cannot carry bets. The 2025 Act defines an e-sport as an organised multiplayer competition decided by skill, recognised under the National Sports Governance Act, 2025 and registered with the Online Gaming Authority, which may charge entry fees and pay prize money but involves no bets or stakes by anyone, player or not. A money game cannot be registered as an e-sport.
Unique to this market.card_text: Esports are a legal category, with no bets
Unique to this market.source: Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act, 2025, section 2(1)(c), MeitY, primary legal text, with the Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Rules, 2026, rule 12(3)

Unique to this market.claim: No Indian law names loot boxes. Neither the 2025 Act nor its 2026 Rules mentions them, and no loot box rule was found elsewhere. When the Online Gaming Authority decides whether a game is a money game it weighs whether money or other stakes are paid in expectation of winning and whether in-game assets can be redeemed or monetised outside the game, so check a game with cash-out or tradeable items against rule 9 before calling it an ordinary video game.
Unique to this market.source: Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Rules, 2026, rule 9, MeitY, primary legal text

Unique to this market.claim: There is no legal cap on how long children play. The 2026 online gaming Rules list time restrictions, age checks and parental controls among the user safety features a game describes when it applies to the Online Gaming Authority, and let the Authority issue codes on user safety, but they set no limit and bind only games that apply or are notified. The government's own summary calls these features mandatory, so read the rule text before quoting either.
Unique to this market.source: Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Rules, 2026, rules 2(1)(i), 6(4) and 23, MeitY, primary legal text

Unique to this market.claim: From 2027, anyone processing an under-18's personal data will need a parent's verifiable consent. The Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 requires it and bars tracking, behavioural monitoring and targeted advertising aimed at children, and rule 10 of the Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025, published on 13 November 2025, sets how the parent is checked. Rule 10 comes into force eighteen months after publication.
Unique to this market.card_text: Parental consent for under-18s' data, from 2027
Unique to this market.source: Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025, G.S.R. 846(E), 13 November 2025, rules 1 and 10, MeitY, primary legal text, with the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, section 9

Unique to this market.claim: The government can block a game outright, and has. On 2 September 2020 the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology blocked 118 mobile apps under section 69A of the Information Technology Act, citing sovereignty, defence, security and public order and data sent to servers outside India. PUBG MOBILE and PUBG MOBILE LITE were among them.
Unique to this market.card_text: Games can be blocked under section 69A
Unique to this market.source: Press Information Bureau, Ministry of Electronics and IT, 2 September 2020, government release

Unique to this market.claim: Blocking orders are not always published, and a block can be lifted. Garena's Free Fire was among 54 apps blocked under section 69A in February 2022 without an official statement, per TechCrunch. Krafton's Battlegrounds Mobile India, blocked in July 2022, was allowed back in May 2023 on a three-month trial after addressing concerns over data security and where its servers were, according to the deputy IT minister as TechCrunch reports.
Unique to this market.card_text: BGMI came back in 2023, on trial
Unique to this market.source: TechCrunch, Manish Singh, 18 May 2023, technology news site, with TechCrunch, 13 February 2022

Unique to this market.claim: Do not describe Indian online games as regulated by industry self-regulatory bodies. The 2023 amendment to the IT Rules let the ministry designate online gaming self-regulatory bodies to verify permissible real-money games, but its obligations for online games apply only three months after at least three such bodies are designated, and no designation could be found. The rule is still in MeitY's consolidated text of 10 February 2026. The 2025 Act and its Online Gaming Authority are the regime in force.
Unique to this market.source: Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021, rules 4A and 4B, updated as on 10 February 2026, MeitY, primary legal text

Unique to this market.claim: The central government backs games through a creative technology institute, not a tax credit. The Indian Institute of Creative Technologies (IICT), a not-for-profit company named the National Centre of Excellence for animation, visual effects, gaming, comics and extended reality (AVGC-XR), opened its first campus in Mumbai on 18 July 2025 with an initial budget of 400 crore rupees, and the Budget 2026-27 speech proposes that it set up AVGC Content Creator Labs in 15,000 secondary schools and 500 colleges.
Unique to this market.card_text: A national institute, not a tax credit
Unique to this market.source: Press Information Bureau explainer, Powering Creative Technology, 18 November 2025, government release, with the Budget 2026-2027 speech, 1 February 2026

Unique to this market.claim: States run their own programmes. Karnataka has an AVGC-XR Policy for 2024 to 2029 on skilling, incubation and market competitiveness, and Maharashtra approved an AVGC-XR Policy in September 2025 with a financial plan of 3,268 crore rupees and a roadmap to 2050, per the central government's account.
Unique to this market.card_text: Karnataka and Maharashtra have AVGC policies
Unique to this market.source: Press Information Bureau explainer, Powering Creative Technology, 18 November 2025, government release

Unique to this market.claim: Android accounted for 92.77 percent of mobile page views in India in August 2026 and iOS for 7.17 percent, per StatCounter, which bases its shares on page views, so the split measures web traffic, not devices, players or spending.
Unique to this market.card_text: Android ~93 percent of mobile web traffic
Unique to this market.source: StatCounter Global Stats, mobile operating system market share in India, August 2026, web analytics

Unique to this market.claim: Google Play in India takes UPI from every provider, including for subscriptions through UPI Autopay, as well as Visa and Mastercard, RuPay cards for one-time purchases, and Play balance and recharge codes. It stopped taking net banking in October 2025.
Unique to this market.card_text: UPI pays for Google Play
Unique to this market.source: Google Play Help, Accepted payment methods on Google Play, India, read 30 September 2026, platform owner's support page

Unique to this market.claim: Do not date the Online Gaming Act from 1 October 2025. The IT minister announced that date in September 2025 and some law-firm notes still give it, but the ministry notified on 22 April 2026 that the Act takes effect from 1 May 2026, the day the Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Rules, 2026 also came into force. The draft rules were published on 2 October 2025.
Unique to this market.source: SCC Online blog, 23 April 2026, legal publisher, reporting the ministry's notification of 22 April 2026

Unique to this market.claim: HOLD: do not report the challenge to the Online Gaming Act as decided. The Supreme Court took the petitions against it from three high courts on 8 September 2025, before a three-judge bench, and no ruling on the Act and no stay of it had been reported by 30 September 2026.
Unique to this market.source: Supreme Court Observer, Challenge to the Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act, 2025, case page, legal tracker

Unique to this market.claim: Do not report the tax demands on real-money gaming companies as stayed. The Supreme Court stayed show-cause notices worth 1.12 lakh crore rupees in January 2025, but on 27 May 2026 it ruled that the 28 percent tax applies to full deposits, and Outlook Business puts the demands for past years that now stand at nearly 2.5 trillion rupees.
Unique to this market.source: Outlook Business, 28 May 2026, business magazine, with LawBeat, January 2025

Where the data lives.claim: FICCI-EY media and entertainment report. The annual report by FICCI and EY sizes India's online and video games, money gaming and esports in rupees, with gamer counts and Sensor Tower genre tables, free to download as a PDF with no form, released each March under a new title.
Where the data lives.source: FICCI and EY, trade body and consultancy annual

Where the data lives.claim: Lumikai State of Interactive Media Report. The games venture fund's annual sizes India's video games, real-money gaming and other interactive media in dollars, with gamer and payer counts and top-grossing titles, free as a PDF on its site with no form. The fifth edition, for calendar 2025, came out on 23 March 2026.
Where the data lives.card_text: Lumikai State of Interactive Media Report
Where the data lives.source: Lumikai, venture fund annual

Where the data lives.claim: Time Use Survey 2024, National Statistics Office (MoSPI). The national survey of how people aged 6 and over spend their day, 139,487 households in 2024 after a first round in 2019, codes play under 823, Playing games and other pastime activities, with no separate code for video games. Free on MoSPI's site.
Where the data lives.source: MoSPI press note, Report: Time Use in India, 2024, 28 March 2025, national statistics office

Where the data lives.claim: Nazara Technologies investor relations. The investors site of the company that calls itself India's only listed gaming company, in business since 1999, carries its quarterly highlights and filings, free.
Where the data lives.source: Nazara Technologies, investor relations site, primary corporate disclosure

Where the data lives.claim: App Store top-grossing games feed, India (Apple). Apple's public RSS feed ranks the top-grossing games in the Indian App Store, free, with prices in rupees and the time of its last update, and a script can read it as JSON. It gives ranks, not revenue, states neither its method nor its period, and covers Apple's store alone.
Where the data lives.card_text: App Store top-grossing games feed, India (Apple)
Where the data lives.source: Apple, iTunes Store RSS feed Top Grossing, Games, India, platform chart

Where the data lives.claim: Google Play top charts for games, India (Google). The games page of Google Play's Indian store shows Top free, Top grossing and Top paid charts for Android, free. It gives ranks only, states no method or period, keeps no archive, and shows the chart for the store's country, set here by gl=IN in the address.
Where the data lives.source: Google Play, games top charts, India, platform chart

Where the data lives.claim: The State of Video Gaming, Matthew Ball and Epyllion. A free annual analyst presentation with market sizing, participation and platform charts for most major markets, useful for cross market comparison that no single free source provides. It aggregates many vendors rather than applying one methodology, so treat figures as the analyst assembly they are and cite the underlying source where the deck names one.
Where the data lives.card_text: The State of Video Gaming (Ball, Epyllion)
Where the data lives.source: Matthew Ball, Epyllion, independent analyst, annual presentation

Where the data lives.claim: There is no games rating database to search in India. The Bureau of Indian Standards' IS 19690:2026, notified on 10 March 2026, sets age ratings from U/A 0+ to A that publishers assess themselves, and it is voluntary, with no order making it compulsory. No public register of ratings under it was found.
Where the data lives.source: Outlook Respawn, Abhimannu Das, 20 April 2026, games news site

known_gaps.gap: Consumer spending. No free figure for what Indian players spend is held: the size card is FICCI-EY's revenue estimate, which counts advertising and esports as well as purchases, and Lumikai's dollar figure is revenue on another basis.
known_gaps.instead: Quote each annual with its edition and basis, as the Market size notes say, and read a spending figure that names no publisher as untraceable.

known_gaps.gap: Player numbers. No count of India's players says who was counted, over what period or how, so the directory carries no player figure for India.
known_gaps.instead: Name the publisher with any count, as the Shape notes do, and use the national Time Use Survey for time spent on games and pastimes, the one official measure.

known_gaps.gap: Company filings. Most of India's largest games companies are private, and only Nazara and OnMobile report games revenue as listed companies.
known_gaps.instead: Use the fiscal-year search technique to find business reporting on private companies' annual filings, and Nazara's and OnMobile's investor pages for the listed ones.

known_gaps.gap: Console and PC play. No chart counts what India plays on console or PC: Steam publishes no chart for India, and both annuals measure phones first.
known_gaps.instead: Read TechEnclave for what PC players buy and pay, and quote a device share only with the annual that states it.

known_gaps.gap: Communities. Most talk among Indian players happens on YouTube, in closed apps, and in Hindi and regional languages, and the open communities held could not be measured or are quiet.
known_gaps.instead: Search YouTube and Discord in Hindi, as the searching tips say, read a Discord server's size from its invite page, and read the forums for the temperature of the talk, never its size.
